**Inventions**
==============
![Image 958: Genshin Impact's Golden Clockwork Meka boss fight, as the pair dances with each other](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2025/01/19/237301566/6652cd2808a2f41f493ac5d24aeab69e_7028453270187602556.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

Fontaine is a technologically advanced nation. One of their most famous inventions is Meks, created by Alain Guillotin and later the Fontaine Research Institute he founded. They were originally clockwork but later began to use Pneumousia energy. Clockwork Meks based on annihilation energy normally produce their energy by utilizing repeaters composed of special crystals to refine ousia and pneuma from Fontaine's environment. But outside of Fontaine, they can use pre-prepared Energy Blocks to move over short distances for short periods. Some Meks are designed for underwater and land-based attacks. For example, the Deepwater Assault Mek was created after the attack of Elynas five hundred years ago. The revered White Armada that sailed upon the great terrestrial lake was completely destroyed in defense of the nation. The designer hoped that were such a thing to happen again, the clockwork meka would possess enough naval firepower to be the first line of defense, going before the soldiers and generals. Other Meks are used for reconnaissance, repair, and construction. One of them was used to build the famous tunnel through Poisson. One of the earliest Meks was the prototype 4ACV07, a thinking Kamera created by Alain Guillotin to protect his sister in the service of the Marechaussee Phantom. One of the most recent Meks was the Experimental Field Generator, created by Edwin Eastinghouse to lift the entire Court of Fontaine into the air and avoid a second flood. Many Meks now stand guard over the Court of Fontaine and belong to the Maison Gardiennage.
Another famous invention of the Fontainians is the Kamera and Film Kamera, created by director and member of the Daydream Club, Xavier. He made some improvements to the Kamera and turned it into a Film Kamera that is also capable of continuously projecting a string of photos, thus creating moving images. In addition to the Film Kamera, Xavier helped create the Mikage Furnace in Inazuma, a machine that can fully utilize the powers of the Tatarigami. When the furnace was damaged by saboteurs from the Sangonomiya troops, he installed a protective dome around it and helped restore it. In addition to Xavier, the club includes Garcia, the creator of the Numbering Machine, Félix Yogue, the inventor of the Evermotion Mechanical Painting, and the brothers Mécantre and Babisse, who are busy building a giant cannon, the projectile of which could reach the very stars of Teyvat, potentially with passengers inside it.

During the existence of the Institute of Natural Philosophy, the predecessor of the Fontaine Research Institute, Mr. Eliphas, who later became the sponsor of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo, worked at the Institute. One of his inventions, which was the result of early forays into optical science by the Institute of Natural Philosophy while they were still a budding academic organization, is the Eliphas Beam. Its basic components include "beam generators" and "beam receivers." The beam generator must sometimes be installed on a "beam receiver" base similar to a regulating valve. It can be controlled and rotated through the use of energy from a Xenochromatic Ball Octopus.

![Image 959: Steampunk-themed airship parked in a green landscape](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2025/01/19/237301566/7589ff656dcb2a466cc9e06c0270bcaa_4269210634180498991.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

In addition to the Meks, the miraculous Antoine Roger Aircraft runs on Pneumousia energy. It's an experimental Aircraft that is propelled by energy generated from pneuma-ousia annihilation reactions. It will proceed along its set route upon being activated. Among Fontaine's many other inventions are the famous Fonta Drink, a flying energy thief, energy transfer terminals, stabilizers, water volume detection crystals, and much more. One of the devices that ran on Indemnitium and produced it was the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale, but after the death of Focalors, this type of energy is no longer available.

Fontaine is also the birthplace of rock and roll. This music is different from the traditional music of other nations, so many are skeptical about it. The Fontaines even organized a musical tour called the "Iridescence Tour," in which a rock singer from Liyue, Xinyan, wanted to perform, but circumstances prevented her. At one of the Lantern Rite Festivals, the main festival of Liyue, the tour organizer Dvorak, with the support of the Qixing, was able to hold a musical event in which Xinyan performed.
_"Rock 'n' roll is a revolution! Transforming your identity and destiny, saying goodbye to concessions and cowardice... it does them all. And most importantly, it lets you do it with art rather than words!_

_My rock 'n' roll has an unbreakable spirit, like a flame in a rainstorm that refuses to go out, or the magma that never stops boiling under the surface of the land."_

**Maison Ordalie**
==================
Fontaine is a nation of justice, so the judicial system plays a central role. Fontaine is headed by the Chief Justice Neuvillette, to whom all the other Maisons report. The judicial system is run by the Maison Ordalie, who attend court cases and pass charges. When Furina was Archon, she often attended court sessions. People could tell the importance of a case by her: if Furina was in court, the case might not be very important, but there was something absurd about it. If the Chief Justice was hearing the case, it would likely be worth attention, but often such cases cannot even be reported to journalists. During Furina's reign, sessions often resembled more of a theatrical performance, but they were still completely subject to the law.

![Image 1019: A character from Genshin Impact named Tartaglia in his Foul Legacy form](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/12/20/237301566/c7ec98269330724afc869375e13cd61c_3704465045727397892.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

All trials take place in the Opera Epiclese, formerly home to the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale, a machine created by the Hydro Archon Focalors. During the trial, the Oratrice and Neuvillette heard the testimony of both sides. The statements of the parties, the speeches of the representatives, the testimonies, and the emotions of the audience were transmitted by the Oratrice, who thus generated the Indemnitium. The Oratrice was like an independent judge, endowed with its own will, whose participation excluded any bias on the part of the Chief Justice. Thanks to this machine and the Chief Justice, false accusations and unfair sentences were almost a thing of the past. At the end of the session, the Chief Justice made the final decision, which the Oratrice took into account. Finally, the officials from the Maison requested the Oratrice's verdict, and its decision was the will of Justice itself. Except for the case when the Oratrice falsely accused the Fatui Harbinger Childe in a serial crime case, there has never been a case where the Chief Justice and the Oratrice disagreed on a verdict. Following the aftermath of Fontaine's prophecy, Neuvillette now rules alone.

![Image 1020: Two Genshin Impact characters with the left one being Neuvillette, sitting on a red and gold seat and the right one being Clorinde, holding a sword, with a torn paper effect dividing them](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/12/20/237301566/11336d37df86e17639e27a7fc9e08a69_6530323178503359102.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

In Fontaine, before a criminal goes to court, they're given one chance to defend their honor by requesting a duel with an official Champion Duelist. The Champion Duelists are all powerful fighters selected from among the nation's best, and the duel itself is a no-holds-barred fight with no specified stopping point. This profession exists to preserve dignity, but it is always accompanied by a struggle. A duel is an open-ended fight that lasts until victory, so participating in such a duel is considered a symbol of the defense of honor. If the criminal manages to win the duel, they will be acquitted, but if they lose, they'll have no choice but to stand trial. Since the challenger can die during the duel, it is usually decided by those who cannot come to terms with an unfair accusation or those who value their honor very much. The only way to end a duel is to surrender or die, and only a few manage to defeat an official Champion Duelist. One of the most famous duelists is the heir of the Marechaussee Hunters — Clorinde. Under her blade, all base actions disguised as the search for justice, and all attempts to gain profit through prosecution reveal their true nature. Clorinde has never known defeat in a duel. One of her most famous duels was the duel with Callas Caspar, president of Spina di Rosula, accused of murdering his friend and informant, Jacques. Before the duel, Callas asked Clorinde to take care of his daughter and Clorinda's friend, Navia, since he was going to die in the duel. Although he was not involved in the murder, he was ready to protect his daughter even at the cost of his life.

**Maison Gardiennage**
======================
![Image 1040: A video game character posing in front of a decorated blue door](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/12/20/237301566/ee15690c48afbc405ad108ec26615e88_9009345316813426973.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

The maintenance of public order in Fontaine is the responsibility of the Maison Gardiennage, based in the Palais Mermonia. The day-to-day defense of the city is the responsibility of the Gardemeks, special Meks created by the Fontaine Research Institute, and they are accompanied by Gardes to assist in patrols. Although the Gardemeks have advanced systems for recognizing criminals, technology is not omnipotent, and there are still many things that only humans can do. The duties of the Maison Gardiennage include protecting the Court of Fontaine and the harbors, solving crimes, finding criminals, and escorting them to Fontaine prison.

![Image 1041: A girl with long purple hair and wearing red military uniform stands on a wooden platform, in the background is a marketplace located in what appears to be a pipe tunnel](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/12/20/237301566/64fc435bece02aabd2f1e780587015ac_265687016241244459.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

If something happens that the Gardes cannot handle, the Special Surveillance and Security Patrol, which reports directly to the Chief Justice, steps in. The Special Patrol is an elite organization within the Maison Gardiennage, and they step in when, for example, prisoners resist or murderers have kidnapped a hostage. All law enforcement officers undergo rigorous background checks and training. Their every word and action represents the Maison Gardiennage and the laws of the Court of Fontaine, so there is no room for error or negligence. However, the way the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol of the Court of Fontaine does things is markedly different from other law enforcement agencies. Members are not required to use standardized weapons, nor must they wear uniforms outside of formal occasions. Additionally, after Chevreuse took command of the Special Patrol, many of its members began using muskets as part of their law enforcement arsenals, and some even began to refuse to go on missions with Gardemeks on the basis that not only can an immobile meka block their line of fire, but there's a distinct danger of criminals taking control of said meka and turning them against the squad. Furthermore, when selecting recruits, the Special Patrol will even accept the descendants of criminals whose households had been stripped of all honor. For the sake of quickly solving the most heinous of cases, the Maison Gardiennage is willing to overlook all those issues, displaying great forbearance towards Chevreuse and the Special Patrol. However, what they simply cannot abide by is how Chevreuse is willing to invite serious felons to participate in cases she is handling as "special consultants." Though Chevreuse stridently maintains that this is purely to catch vicious criminals as soon as possible, many colleagues still believe that relying on lawbreakers to help arrest lawbreakers is an insult to both the laws of Fontaine and those who enforce them.
There is a horror story for naughty children in Fontaine: _"If you don't behave, the Special Patrol's going to take you away!"_ Although children understand very clearly that the Special Patrol will never take action because a child didn't brush their teeth, it is difficult for them to suppress an involuntary shudder at the sight of the Special Patrol officers. The officers themselves are irritated by this bad reputation since it can damage their image. The Special Patrol is the official law enforcement unit of the Maison Gardiennage, and if their methods of law enforcement are harsher and the process itself more intense, it is only because the criminals they deal with are the most dangerous of all. Once, the officers even offered their captain, Chevreuse, an interview with The Steambird, but she declined the offer. _"If such a reputation has really become so deeply embedded in the minds of the people, and it sticks with them for a lifetime, then there's a chance that when someone considers taking things a step too far, fear inspired by our 'infamous reputation' may pull them back from the edge. If so, then there'll be no need for us to actually take them away someday."_

![Image 1042: Three characters from Genshin Impact stand in front of stained glass and candles; the middle character holds a sword while the character on the right holds a bow](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/06/07/237301566/b083eea6dc2eb3aa30a08919b7df4fd5_5069936352409982939.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

Another special elite organization that is part of the Maison Gardiennage and directly subordinate to the Chief Justice is the Marechaussee Phantom. The Marechaussee Phantom originated from the Marechaussee Hunters — the surviving Remurians who, under the leadership of the Harmost Cassiodor, fought the remnants of the sunken empire. The Marechaussee Phantom used to be entirely human, but now the majority are Melusines. When the Chief Justice discovered that the Melusines' unique "sight" helped in investigations, they began to be recruited to help, even though they were not strong in combat. The most significant cases in the history of the Marechaussee Phantom are the Siege of Poisson and the Battle in Elynas, during which many people died.

![Image 1043: Pearl motif with seashell and swirl design](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/02/15/237301566/c7324129b0223e4112132db8b48999f7_6667263520141079544.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

The emblem of the Maison Gardiennage depicts two Melusines. When the Chief Justice Neuvillette first brought the Melusines to the Court of Fontaine, Carole became the first Melusine in the Marechaussee Phantom. Thanks to their five years of hard work, Carole was awarded the first Medal of Peace created personally by Neuvillette. This medal further angered the supporters of the old regime, who were against the Melusines in the Court of Fontaine and whose interests were infringed upon as a result of Neuvillette's reform. They decided to commit murder and blame it on the Melusines to drive them out of the city and teach Neuvillette a lesson. They tricked Carole into coming to the crime scene and brought charges against her. After this, they sowed panic among the people in order to force Neuvillette to admit his mistakes and give up power. Carole decided to sacrifice herself to soften the situation, and the Gardes were unable to intervene in time due to the angry crowd. Carole's bravery and sacrifice ultimately led to her dream being realized: four hundred years later, the Melusines are respected members of society in the Court of Fontaine, coexisting peacefully with humans. Because of Carole's heroic deed, the emblem of the Maison Gardiennage featured Melusines as a sign of respect and gratitude to these creatures.

**Maison Cardinalice**
======================
Like the Maison Gardiennage, the Maison Cardinalice is located in the heart of the Court of Fontaine, the Palais Mermonia. They are responsible for all of Fontaine's finances and administrative affairs, including the planning of the aquabus lines and the distribution of funds. It was the Maison Cardinalice that announced Furina's appointment as an Archon 500 years ago. They also collect the various proposals and issue official replies thanking the Fontainians for their help. In order to allocate funds to the needs of the Maisons, the employees of these Maisons first collect receipts for a month, and then at the end of the month, they are submitted to the Maison Cardinalice for verification. The approval process is linked to the approval and payment of salaries to all employees. If the expenditure is too large, the Maison Cardinalice will have to contact Monsieur Neuvillette himself. And if Monsieur Neuvillette has questions about any of the expenditure items, the employee in question will also have to write an explanation. The staff of other Maisons believe that the Maison Cardinalice too often states that all explanatory notes are a personal demand of Neuvillette.

The Maison Gestion, located in the Palais Mermonia, handles all of Fontaine's paperwork and is notorious for its bureaucracy. Many young employees join the Maison full of enthusiasm for helping others but are confronted with an endless number of rules and different departments. At first, they believe that the Maison Gestion should be a fair, efficient, and strong organization in which everyone would help each other, and under its management, the Court of Fontaine would prosper. But then they see that the Maison is like the ruins of a mechanical building: people chaotically pull levers and press random buttons, and only its outer appearance remains decent. Many new employees leave, unable to withstand such work, but others change, having found their place in the system. Among the rules of the Maison Gestion is a rule that all their correspondence must be delivered by mail. And even if the sender and recipient are opposite each other, it is necessary to use the mail. This approach is called "traceability."

**Fortress of Meropide**
========================
![Image 1068: Underwater stylized fantasy scene with a mechanical tower complex in the center](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/12/20/237301566/35b91b0f4bded29a18df0855fb35c083_3340048922706017865.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

When Egeria ruled the land, all convicted criminals from Fontaine were exiled. The people drove the criminals away like a wolf pack chasing away the banished. The criminals received no sympathy of any kind from the people. They were exiled to the desolate seaside, where they experienced only pain, struggle, and the bone-chilling cold. Some of them began to repent, and prayed to the Hydro Archon, asking if there was still anything they could do. The Hydro Archon took pity on them, and said: _"You may go guard my secret, deep underneath the waves."_ Leaning on her power, they gathered under the sea and began building a fortress, forming a community that grew over the years and guarding the seal to the Primordial Sea.
When the first group of exiles died, they left the unfinished fortress to their successors. The Hydro Archon continued to support them, allowing the fortress to grow and thrive. This dark underwater fortress became the only home for the sinners. They no longer saw it as a prison but as a place of repentance, hoping to regain their freedom through redemption. However, as time passed, they realized the Fortress was a lonely place. Once accustomed to life there, they could no longer feel comfortable in the overworld. Some left after serving their sentences, while others stayed, finding idle positions and letting their souls fade away with ancient secrets. The number of those who joined the order and lived underwater gradually grew, while those who took the oath with understanding and knowledge of the teachings steadily diminished. After many centuries, few remembered the original reason for the Fortress's founding. Now, it is seen as an integral part of Fontainian society, and a gathering place for exiles.

The Fortress is an underwater stronghold with a measure of autonomy and self-governance from Fontaine's legal systems. Despite being autonomous, it serves as a prison for those who have stood trial and been sentenced. Different people of different backgrounds come here for all kinds of reasons. They can live peaceful, regimented lives, free from fear — no matter what they've gone through. The Fortress of Meropide is ruled by Duke Wriothesley, who was once an inmate there himself. During the prophecy's fruition, he and his flying ship provided invaluable assistance to the Fontainians, saving them from the flood. Moreover, the Fortress is the main factory for the Meks' production.

**Soloist's Prologue**
----------------------
![Image 1078: Cliffside settlement on the coast with waterfalls, mountains, and boats in the water](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/07/09/237301566/dedd60ac6dbe044331c6cfd8906cfe4b_466460870954823315.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

After a long adventure in Sumeru, the Traveler and Paimon said goodbye to their friends and embarked on a journey to Fontaine, the nation of Hydro. Their main goal was to meet with the Hydro Archon, Furina. After talking with locals, including the magician Lyney and his sister and assistant, Lynette, in Romaritime Harbor, they learned about the peculiarities of the trials in Fontaine, which are more like theatrical performances, and about Miss Furina. Although she was an Archon, for the people of Fontaine she was more of a star and a "mascot." The Traveler and Paimon were about to leave for the Court of Fontaine when the Hydro Archon herself appeared to greet them:
_"I've long heard of the turmoil and chaos you've left in your wake as you visited other nations, but I welcome you nevertheless... No, I have come to receive you personally."_

_"You may consider this my reward to all of you! I have determined that there will be an epic duel between myself and this traveler from another land, just as you were hoping to see!"_

When the Traveler agreed to a duel, Furina pretended that the spectators were tired of mere duels and decided to face them in court, accusing them of a crime: _"According to Fontaine law, no one is permitted to release any flying objects within Fontaine city limits during the first three days of each month."_ Their new acquaintance Lyney, who foresaw this outcome of events, came to the aid of the Traveler and Paimon. Upon meeting Paimon, he touched her back to quietly connect her with a rope to the Traveler's hand. Furina dropped the charges and left not to attract attention to her failed accusations, leaving the Traveler with Lyney and Lynette. They spoke about a prophecy that people in Fontaine had known about for a long time.

_"It says that every person in Fontaine is born with 'sin.' No matter how the Nation of Justice holds trial after trial, this sin cannot be absolved._

_Until one day, the water levels in Fontaine will rise, and the sinful people will slowly be drowned..._

_In the end, the people will all be dissolved into the waters, and only the Hydro Archon will remain, weeping on her throne... Only then will the sins of the people of Fontaine be washed away."_

![Image 1079: Archon character from Genshin Impact, known as Focalors, sits on a throne surrounded by submerged ruins](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/07/09/237301566/43c0c138c40111c11fe4bcf63ed89e5b_6109125312260281233.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

To prepare the Fontainians for the flood, the siblings gave the people Magic Pockets that could hold all their belongings. As Lyney and Lynette were about to accompany the Traveler and Paimon to the Court of Fontaine, they noticed a suspicious girl who was creating a distraction to rob people. Lyney wanted to detain her but lost sight of her when he twisted an ankle, and she abandoned the stolen things.

On the aquabus on the way to the Court of Fontaine, the Traveler and Paimon met their old friend from the grand tournament of the "Genius Invokation TCG," journalist Charlotte. She wanted to write about the case of serial disappearances that everyone in Fontaine was talking about. For 20 years, someone has been kidnapping young women of the same age, who have disappeared without a trace. Many suspects have been arrested over the years, but after each arrest, a new disappearance would occur.

**The City of Rains and Remembrance**
-------------------------------------
In the Court of Fontaine, Lyney and Lynette introduced the Traveler to their brother, Freminet. When it suddenly began to rain, Freminet spoke of the legend: Fontaine was once ruled by the Hydro Dragon, and every time the dragon cried, the sky became clouded and rain poured down. To stop the rain, you had to shout into the sky: _"Hydro dragon, Hydro dragon, don't cry!"_

![Image 1097: Tartaglia, a video game character from Genshin Impact, lying with his eyes closed in the dark](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/07/09/237301566/1638cb9d4af2d686eba8d4741d2e5bb2_2852378782467521304.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

While picking up materials for the Magic Pockets from the Beaumont Workshop, the Traveler and Paimon saw the Fatui Harbinger,

Childe,Tartaglia

collecting debts from members of Confrerie of Cabriere. Delighted with his acquaintance, he spoke about his stay in Fontaine, but members of the association did not allow him to finish. During the fight with them, it turned out that Tartaglia's Hydro abilities began to refuse to obey him. Childe began to have the feeling that a restless power was stirring inside of him. Paimon and Tartaglia suggested that this could be due to problems with the Vision. Childe said that when he was fourteen, he fell into an unknown abyss. There, Childe had a dream where he was in the deepest depths of the sea, and the boundless seabed was all around him. A massive whale appeared in front of him and was forever stuck in his memory. Having fallen into the abyss, Tartaglia met Skirk, who became his master and taught him combat techniques. She told him that he had awakened "it," and traces of "it" remained on him. When Tartaglia got out of the abyss, he did not stop looking for his master for an answer, but he never found anything. In order not to rely on his Vision, Childe entrusted it to the Traveler, leaving the Delusion for himself.
After meeting Childe, the Traveler and Paimon went to the Opera Epiclese on Erinnyes to watch Lyney and Lynette's performance. When the Traveler was approaching the Fountain of Lucine, they suddenly heard a voice calling for Vacher due to their sensitivity to Hydro. Lynette said that tears containing a person's most vivid emotions flowed into the Fountain of Lucine, so that the Traveler could hear these emotions.

![Image 1098: An exploded cube with gold lining is surrounded by splinters in a body of water in the style of concept art](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/07/09/237301566/6dc55c573383e53704eafbb4d8634024_7460978121142764148.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

During the performance, Lyney decided to perform a swapping trick. Lyney and a spectator selected by a random number generator each had to enter their magic box and after a minute switch places. The number generator chose a young woman, Halsey. There was a noise during the countdown, but the audience didn't pay much attention to it. When the minute came to an end, a tank of water suddenly fell onto the box from which the spectator was supposed to emerge, crushing it. Instead of Halsey, the box contained Lyney's assistant, Cowell. Since the woman disappeared without a trace, just like in a disappearance case, Furina, who was present at the performance, immediately announced Lyney as the main suspect in this case. The Archon could not retract her words in front of the public, so a trial began in which the Traveler and Paimon had to defend Lyney.

**Lies Cast Shadows Under Gathered Lights**
-------------------------------------------
During the investigation, it turned out that the rope holding the water tank was deliberately replaced with another one made of flammable materials. Fireworks set off shortly before the end of the performance ignited the rope and caused the water tank to collapse onto the box. The random number generator that chose Halsey always showed a certain number, and the girl was chosen deliberately.

While leaving the theater after collecting evidence, the Traveler and Paimon encountered Navia, the head of Spina di Rosula. She followed the disappearance case closely, and Lyney did not seem suitable for the role of the criminal. Navia proposed to team up to exonerate Lyney and solve the disappearance case. Together, they learned that there was a secret passage under the magic boxes connecting them. Inside the box was another smaller one, and during the performance, it was supposed to lower itself and ride on a cart through a tunnel. Spilled water and the clothes of the missing woman were found in the passage.

![Image 1122: The Scales of Justice, with a blue water drop on each side and one on top, stands in a chamber, decorated in gold and pink](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/07/09/237301566/f9637e460d788f9ba3c8144200245850_7030646470507962620.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

At the trial, Furina pointed out Lyney's deception: he claimed that he only heard the countdown, but during it, there was a noise that could not be heard while in the box. In addition, she announced that Lyney and Lynette grew up in the House of the Hearth and were Fatui, which instantly led spectators to believe that the magician was guilty. It turned out that to prevent the prophecy, Lyney was trying to find out how the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale, a special device in the courtroom that makes verdicts, worked. Lyney and Lynette figured out that Oratrice's core was below the stage, so they chose the swap trick to end up near it. During the countdown, Lyney went down into the tunnel, reached the basement through the ventilation passage, and went to explore the room in which the core was stored. When he reached the desired room, he heard someone's voice, which recognized Lyney and tried to talk to him. The magician decided not to take any risks and left the same way he came.
The evidence obtained led the Traveler to believe that the deceased Cowell was involved in the crime himself. He knew how Lyney's trick worked and had access to the props. After examining Cowell's personal belongings, several vials of liquid were discovered, labeled as "Water of the Primordial Sea." According to entries in his notebook, Cowell was part of a group that trafficked in illegal substances and had an accomplice. One of the tubes labeled "Opera Epiclese" with the date of the performance was empty. The notebook mentioned the safe usage of the water of the Primordial Sea and the dissolution. The notes also stated that these dissolution properties work exclusively on people from Fontaine.

![Image 1123: A collage illustration depicting a woman running from danger](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/07/09/237301566/0f3bddb2f5c8289bb5492ca5e7e8e77e_5520667465853318273.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

A test tube with water was also found in Lyney's personal effects. Furina was ready to win the lawsuit, but suddenly Navia introduced the missing girl. She was not an artist Halsey, but a thief Liliane, whom the Traveler, Lyney, and Lynette met in Romaritime Harbor. She heard about the performance of a famous magician and stole a ticket. After receiving the list of spectators, Cowell selected a victim and hacked the random number generator. To cover up any evidence after dissolving the woman, Cowell decided to allow the water tank to fall. He tampered with the ropes suspending the water tank so they would burst under fireworks at the end of the performance. While preparing the props for the performance, he arranged everything so that the water of the Primordial Sea would pour over the girl as she descended into the tunnel in the box. If everything had gone according to plan, the girl in the box would have disappeared into the water. However, Liliane was from Mondstadt, and thus she remained unharmed and opened the box with a loud knock. Realizing that the girl had not disappeared, Cowell went down into the tunnel, and a fight broke out between them. Liliane was able to knock Cowell unconscious and push him into the magic box, then changed her clothes and hid in the props box.
Thanks to the investigation of the Traveler, Paimon, and Navia, Lyney was acquitted, but Neuvillette drew attention to the presence of a test tube with water in the magician's belongings. One of the Gardes was Cowell's accomplice, who was mentioned in the notebook. He was ordered to place the blame for the disappearances on Lyney and direct the blame to Fatui. When the Garde was ready to testify against his boss, he was dissolved.

During a break in court, Lyney apologized for hiding his affiliation with the House of the Hearth and explained how he and his sister joined Fatui. When their parents died, he and Lynette ended up on the streets. To survive, Lyney took to surreptitiously observing an older street performer who did magic. Within a few days, the boy figured out how amazing tricks were pulled, and the siblings began performing tricks in a crowded place. Although the performances allowed them to earn them food, they were left without a home. One day, an aristocrat approached them and offered to adopt them. He would constantly take children to banquets and parties to garner attention, which he would then use to expand his social circles. After one of the performances, Lyney noticed that Lynette was not around, to which the aristocrat replied that she caught the eye of a most eminent person at the banquet, so he sent her over as a gift. Lyney managed to ferret out the location of the mansion of that so-called "eminent person," but when he made his way inside, he only saw the bloody floor and the silhouette of

The Knave Arlecchino

standing there in the darkness. The Harbinger rescued Lynette and discovered several girls in the basement of the house. Arlecchino promised that children would never be betrayed in the House of the Hearth, and the siblings joined her. Together they planned to destroy the prophecy and save Fontaine.
As Traveler and Paimon were leaving the theater, they encountered Navia. She suggested that they continue to investigate the case of serial disappearances, but the Traveler refused. Navia accepted the refusal and proposed a farewell dinner to celebrate the completion of the collaboration.

======================================
**Like the Faint Moonlight of Yesteryear**
------------------------------------------
During a farewell dinner with Navia after completing cooperation on the dissolution case at the Opera Epiclese, the Traveler, Paimon, and Navia reflected on the case and discussed a possible meeting with Furina. Paimon accidentally drank Navia's Fonta, and her and the Traveler's drink was salty and tasteless. When the Traveler and Paimon were returning home, near the Fountain of Lucine, they heard a strange voice calling Vacher again. The Traveler contacted a mysterious Oceanid, who asked them to tell Vacher not to look for her anymore. A long time ago, this Oceanid was a human, Vigneire: she visited many places, loved adventures, and explored places of peril. Wherever she went, her beloved Vacher was always nearby. One day she was covered in light blue water, and she was "released" from her body: there was no more fear nor frenzy, with only an endless peace, like the water's still surface. This state is similar to being a thirsty person who drinks water for the first time, and only then sees how they have lived for so long in a world of endless want and anxiety. Her memories were washed away like a flood, and many fragments dissolved amidst the tide, never to be recovered.

![Image 1143: Many golems stand in front of the forest and men](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/08/24/237301566/4eaa20e22f590c6c4d2adb1e476f3bc2_8540823915471733868.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

When the Traveler woke up from this vision, they saw defeated Meks along with the Champion Duelist Clorinde, Navia, and Paimon, who looked scared. After the dinner Navia realized that the salty Fonta Paimon drank tasted different because of the water of the Primordial Sea and that the drink was intended for herself. Her performance during the trial attracted the attention of the powerful organization behind the dissolution of the women, so they decided to get rid of her. Navia's father, Callas, died in a legal duel at the hands of Clorinde, and before the fight, he asked her to ensure the safety of his daughter. Clorinde believed that danger had been following her old friend lately, so she followed her to the Fountain of Lucine and arrived just in time to save the Traveler, Navia, and Paimon. All the attacking Gardemeks did not have serial numbers, which only very rich and influential people could afford.

![Image 1144: A steampunk style emblem of a ship anchor with roses hanging on a brown colored wall with pipes and metallic elements](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/08/24/237301566/ae577647454167a7a0f797a6a7dc5603_6413261362752492789.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

After surviving the attack, the Traveler and Paimon decided to join Navia's investigation. For safety reasons, Spina di Rosula invited them to spend the night at one of their bases in the Fleuve Cendre. After the death of the previous head of the Spina, Callas Caspar, known as "Callas the Unfaithful," the organization became strapped for funds. They did not allow illegal or unethical profit-making and often relied on funds from residents who supported them. Three years earlier, Navia's father was accused of murdering a friend, but he chose a duel to defend his honor rather than face trial. Navia hoped that if he appeared in court and the investigation was carried out properly, then there would be inconsistencies that would prove his innocence, but Callas asked for a duel and refused to surrender, deciding to die. Three years later, Navia continued to investigate her father's death and the disappearance case she believed her father was handling before the trial.
During a sleepless night, Navia continued to investigate the involvement of a man named Vacher in the disappearance case. She researched all available sources, but his name was erased from the face of the earth and was not mentioned anywhere. She believed that those behind the dissolutions had already taken steps to permanently remove the name of a key witness from history. The last ray of hope in their investigation was to be the archives of the Chief Justice Neuvillette, where detailed information on all cases in recent years could be found.

**The Truth, Lost With the Rain**
---------------------------------
At the Palais Mermonia, Navia pretended that she was going to report and archive some information on a follow-up case in order to get to the Сhief Justice. After looking through all the archives, Neuvillette did not find a single mention of Vacher. In parting, he expressed regret over the death of Navia's father, but she rejected his sympathy:

_"In your eyes, the value of a human life is nothing compared to those cold laws you hold so dear._

_Why didn't you... give me the power to stop him from throwing his life away, why did you just let him die, despised and hated by all…_

_If you really have no heart, then just look me in the eyes — I, Navia, will show you the true meaning of 'regret'!"_

When Navia was leaving Neuvillette, it suddenly started to rain, and she remembered that on the day of the murder which Callas was accused for, it also rained. New evidence about people being dissolved could mean that the real killer could have turned into water and been washed away by the rain. In Poisson, the home of Spina di Rosula, Navia and the Traveler identified three suspects who could be behind the murder of Callas's friend Jacques: Spina di Rosula's senior adviser, Florian; the Garde responsible for cooperation between the organization and the Maison Gardiennage, Thierry; and the head of Spina di Rosula's subsidiary, the Confrerie of Cabriere, Marcel. After talking with them, Jacques's wife, and Melus, Navia, and the Traveler received new evidence.

About 20 years ago, Fontaine was confronted with the disappearance of young women. Despite all the efforts of the Maison Gardiennage, neither the women nor the criminal was ever found. In addition, a few years ago in Poisson, a certain Sinthe began to gain popularity — a drink that could excite one's mood and produce many pleasant hallucinations. With long-term use of Sinthe, many side effects occurred, including a loss of the ability to focus or control one's emotions. Upon withdrawal, the person experienced flashes of paranoia and anxiety while lacking the energy to do anything. Sinthe itself was the diluted water of the Primordial Sea which was capable of dissolving the Fontainians.

![Image 1164: Comic panels show the character from The Great Ace Attorney at a birthday celebration, lying injured in the woods, and in a police station](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/08/24/237301566/a4f32cb7b9aad3d2c1ee8f191c2b09cd_5236637881673344349.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

Callas, who was the head of Poisson at the time, demanded a complete ban on Sinthe and decided to find the person behind the sale of the drink. Realizing that the enemy was intelligent, Callas decided to secretly establish contact with the sellers and build personal relationships with them. Eventually, he managed to convince one man, Jacques, to become his informant. Jacques was ashamed of his work after seeing the effects of Sinthe, so he agreed to help Callas. One evening, Callas held a banquet at a countryside estate, where he planned to exchange information with Jacques. That day he was cheerful, drinking and joking with everyone at the table, and then went out to get some fresh air, leaving his weapon on the table. Suddenly, two shots were heard, and on the spot, people found Callas holding a gun in his hands and Jacques dead on the ground. For lack of other evidence, Callas was accused of murder and called "Callas the Unfaithful." At his trial, he chose a duel and refused to surrender, resulting in his death. When the president of Spina di Rosula was accused of murder, the organization lost its influence.
Callas had discovered the connection between Sinthe and the case of the missing women long before that evening. According to the information received, the next victim was supposed to be Navia, Callas's daughter, and he could not stay away. Knowing that due to an incurable illness, he did not have enough time to complete the investigation he had begun, Callas decided to take extreme measures. He stated that he had important evidence in his hands, incriminating the criminals and known to members of Spina di Rosula. But as long as his daughter was safe, the evidence would not be made public. Since Callas was afraid that something would threaten his daughter, he did not deny his guilt in the murder of Jacques and chose to die on a Duelists' Ring. Before his death, he shared the location of the Sinthe factory with Melus.

The only one who could be behind the crime was Marcel since he had sufficient influence and wealth. When Navia and the Traveler were about to be sent to the Sinthe production base, news arrived that a serial dissolutions trial had begun at the Opera Epiclese, in which the Fatui Harbinger, Tartaglia, was accused. Since the disappearances began when Tartaglia was just a child, the charges seemed absurd, but if they remained in force, it would no longer be possible to convince the Gardes to support the investigation into Callas. To find out the whole truth, Navia went to court to press charges against Marcel, and Traveler and Paimon went to the Sinthe production base.

**When All Return to the Waters**
---------------------------------
![Image 1188: A steampunk-style room is rendered in blue and green tones with gears and plants](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/08/24/237301566/5419631f4e8f3e738d71c2bb91a2bf5a_2782653288336996690.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

While exploring an underwater laboratory for the production of Sinthe, the Traveler and Paimon discovered the source of the Primordial Sea, evidence of the production of Sinthe, a report on Callas, a log of experiments on the revival of dissolved people, and the personal belongings of the missing women. It turned out that Vacher was an adventurer from Snezhnaya who, during his journey to Fontaine, met and fell in love with another adventurer, Vigneire. During one of their underwater expeditions, Vigneire came in contact with the water of the Primordial Sea, which dissolved her in front of Vacher. He was so devastated by her death, that he tried to reunite with his beloved, but the water of the Primordial Sea did not cause him any harm, since he was a native of Snezhnaya. For many years, Vacher sought help from the officers of the Maison Gardiennage, but they told him that humans couldn't turn into water and that he went mad out of grief. He felt that Vigneire's death was brushed away by all of them as if it didn't matter at all.

![Image 1189: Steampunk-themed interior with a blue and gold color scheme, featuring large gears, a central monument, and ornate detailing, lit by shafts of light](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/08/24/237301566/8e613d6a279e9b6aecd32197080c788d_9198948766632311810.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

In desperation, Vacher began to look for ways to bring Vigneire back. One day he found the notes left by Jakob Ingold, a member of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo, who had conducted experiments using the Primordial waters many years ago, and decided to use this research in his experiments. Vacher began kidnapping Fontainian women the same age as Vigneire in an attempt to revive his beloved. To remain above suspicion, Vacher decided to get rid of his old identity and came up with a story about a businessman, Marcel, who had just arrived in Fontaine. He found the name Marcel in Vigneire's diary, where she was choosing names for her and Vacher's children. During his research, Marcel noticed that a small amount of Primordial Sea water, diluted in ordinary water, is not lethal even for the inhabitants of Fontaine, but has intoxicating properties. Marcel named this drink Sinthe and started an underground business producing it.
In court, Navia accused Marcel of involvement in the death of her father, Callas, and the disappearance case, but could not prove his guilt. Then she asked to reopen the case related to the murder of Jacques. According to new data, Callas did not give an explanation in court about the disappearance of the women, since his daughter could become the next victim. Even if the Gardes eventually figured out what was going on, it would be too late. Additionally, the Champion Duelist Clorinde confirmed that Callas had no intention of leaving the ring alive to defend the truth. Neuvillette and Furina agreed to reopen the case, but they could not understand the connection between it and the disappearance case. These two cases were connected by the factor of time: to kill Jacques and Callas, as well as to dissolve the Garde during Lyney's trial, the criminal had to be at both crime scenes, and it was Marcel who was present at both the banquet and the courtroom. Marcel denied these accusations, saying that when the disappearances of the girls began, he was in Snezhnaya, and arrived in Fontaine only later. When it seemed that Navia had no arguments left, she asked if he remembered the name Vacher.

![Image 1190: An image of a blue-tinged scene featuring a translucent spirit or energy-based entity that has a bright, orb-like core with crystalline-shaped structures around it. There are also several people, drawn in an anime style, standing around the spirit, contributing to the mystical and ethereal feeling](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/08/24/237301566/d5998d077443b38b8c3b0eaea1c5530d_8306747509658970845.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

The Traveler, who arrived in court in time, presented the evidence found in the laboratory, and Marcel no longer denied his guilt. The Chief Justice Neuvillette, as well as the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale, a special device created by the Hydro Archon, Focalors, found Marcel guilty. During the trial, Marcel asked the Traveler how they found out his real name. After he learned about the story of the mysterious voice, he asked the Gardes to take him to the Fountain of Lucine before the imprisonment. Thanks to the water of the Primordial Sea, he contacted the voice, hoping that it was his beloved, but it turned out to be the consciousness of all the women whom Marcel had dissolved for over 20 years. Marcel was desperate to see Vigneire, but every tendril of her consciousness was avoiding him. From the moment his first victim died, and her consciousness merged with Vigneire's, she had nothing but pure hatred for Marcel. In the vision, the women attacked Marcel with the desire to kill him, but in reality, Marcel seemed to have lost his soul. The doctor's report stated that Marcel died from severe fright.
It would seem that the case of the serial disappearance of the women was completely solved, but the Oratrice made an unexpected verdict and accused Fatui Harbinger, Tartaglia, of being guilty of this case. As the Oratrice's verdicts were crucial, the Gardemeks were supposed to escort the Harbinger to the Fortress of Meropide. Using the Delusion, Tartaglia attacked the Gardemeks, but the Chief Justice defeated him, promising to find out the whole truth.

**A Tea Party Most Thorny**
---------------------------
![Image 1214: Arlecchino sitting at a table with a teacup, a lamp, and her hand under her chin](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/11/14/237301566/bcd22c2364dddfabdd2d02d5d2dc0ee0_7694349253952398989.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

Since the case of the serial disappearances had been solved, the Traveler and Paimon headed back to the Spina di Rosula base in the Court of Fontaine to have a rest. After a few days, they met with Monsieur Neuvillette who informed them that earlier, the Snezhnayan Harbinger, The Knave, had sought a diplomatic meeting with Furina. He had suggested declining the invitation outright, as he found the request to be abrupt and likely connected to Childe's recent arrest and imprisonment in the Fortress of Meropide. Despite Neuvillette's reservations, Furina insisted on pursuing the meeting, trusting Neuvillette's ability to navigate any issues that arose. Neuvillette agreed to assist, sensing there might be more to the Hydro Archon's motivations.

The Knave Arlecchino

suggested viewing their meeting as an ordinary tea party, downplaying its diplomatic nature. Furina revealed she had invited Neuvillette, who was acknowledged by The Knave as a respected figure in Fontaine. Arlecchino expressed gratitude for Furina and Neuvillette's efforts to improve the lives of the House of the Hearth's children, although she made it clear she wasn't referring to her children Lyney and Lynette, who were falsely accused by Furina. The Chief Justice shifted the conversation to the matter of Childe, as he understood the Harbinger's situation was indeed one of the goals of The Knave's trip. Arlecchino requested the Harbinger be turned over to Snezhnaya, citing their diplomatic roles and responsibilities. However, since the trial was concluded, Fontaine saw the case as settled, and Neuvillette denied her request. The Knave then proposed visiting the Fortress of Meropide to check on Childe, but the Fortress of Meropide fell outside the court's jurisdiction. Hence, the Chief Justice offered an alternative proposal. Not long before the meeting, Childe had vanished from the Fortress, with no sightings reported outside. Arlecchino reluctantly accepted the proposal to send someone to the Fortress to investigate. The Traveler and Paimon were best suited to do so due to their familiarity with Childe along with the unique nature of the Fortress of Meropide, along with the Fortress's autonomy. Neuvillette arranged for them to gain access to the prison by framing them with false charges, which they agreed to, to maintain secrecy. As they left, he offered them a cake as "a token of gratitude."
The Traveler and Paimon went to Café Lutece to enjoy their last day of freedom and Charlotte, a journalist, interrupted them. She asked for help with a story about Wriothesley, the fortress's warden who was awarded the rare title of "Duke" in Fontaine. Paimon agreed when Charlotte offered to cover their meal expenses in return.

Later, accompanied by the Iudex, they reached the entrance of the underwater prison. Due to both the barrier of the water as well as the fear humans have of the depths, the Fortress of Meropide is the perfect place to confine and guard criminals. When the Traveler and Paimon reached their destination, they met a woman who was personally requested to escort them by Monsieur Neuvillette. The charge against the pair was consuming the cake they had been offered earlier, as the cake was intended for Furina, and they were sentenced to 45 days of imprisonment. Considering how fond Lady Furina is of sweets, this crime is said to have been tantamount to trying to assassinate the Hydro Archon herself. An inmate arrived shortly after to guide them inside the Fortress.

**Fortress of Meropide**
------------------------
![Image 1234: Inside view of a corridor in what seems to be a clockwork factory with multiple humanoid robots standing on both sides, with a huge gear at the end of the corridor](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/11/14/237301566/f43cc111ff0c95bba9cc967098a92ca6_187391763835543753.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

While entering the fortress, the Traveler and Paimon noticed there were many Gardemeks present. Wriothesley, the Duke, met the Traveler and Paimon and addressed them as prisoners number 7459 and 7560 and reassured them that the Gardemeks present were not hostile; rather, they served as their "honor guard." He then invited them to follow him on a tour of the various facilities in the Fortress of Meropide to ease their transition into their new life. 

![Image 1235: Interior view of a large room with stone walls, and a giant fan in the background, with pipes along the wall, plus a character in the lower right corner](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/11/14/237301566/887c430dd341d1e2f5d2f2989e5514dc_3265373861925249671.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

The tour began at the Coupon Cafeteria, where each inmate is guaranteed a daily welfare meal, a policy introduced by the Duke to ensure no one goes hungry. Before his administration, even necessities like water required Credit Coupons, and new inmates had to work without food until they earned enough coupons. Next, Wriothesley introduced the Pankration Ring, a space for inmates to participate in voluntary matches to release extra energy and earn additional coupons. Wriothesley approved the ring's construction, receiving a share of the profits to maintain safety and manage conflicts. The tour continued to the dormitories, where inmates sleep, and the Production Zone, where they work to earn Credit Coupons, though some can opt out if they have alternative skills. During this stop, they spotted Lyney at the fortress but decided to keep quiet. Luckily, Wriothesley viewed him as just another inmate. The next stop was the infirmary, where they met Sigewinne, the head nurse who manages the facility alone. Afterward, they returned to the cafeteria for a meal, which Sigewinne noted was chosen at random, depending on luck.
During the meal, Wriothesley explained that all kinds of mechanical products for official use, and some essential goods, have to be obtained from the overworld, so naturally, Neuvillette and Wriothesley have to stay in touch. Per the Duke's instructions, the Traveler and Paimon headed back to the dormitories to rest. After the day's events, they started to suspect that Wriothesley knew about their plan with Neuvilette and that Lyney was also conducting an investigation into Tartaglia's disappearance. Just then, they noticed a magician's card lying on a box nearby. As they went to investigate, they noticed a message, which read _"It was nice to bump into you again. Let's catch up in the production zone tomorrow."_

The next day, the Traveler and Paimon arrived at the Production Zone and made widgets in exchange for Credit Coupons. Afterwards, they met with Lyney and Lynette who informed the Traveler and Paimon that Freminet was also at the Fortress. They ended up at the Fortress due to charges of theft after their street performance ended with the disappearance of their audience's wallets, and instructed by the "Father" of the House of the Hearth, The Knave Arleccino, to investigate the secret of the Fortress of Meropide was hiding. The House of the Hearth had been investigating for a very long time, trying to uncover the mystery, when all of their informants, including the ones that had infiltrated the guards, suddenly vanished. Additionally, "Father" had somehow managed to confirm that Focalors did not have the Hydro Gnosis. It was this information that led them to suspect that Fontaine's Gnosis might be in the Fortress of Meropide, and related to that "secret." Arleccino was merely using Childe's disappearance to put pressure on Furina.

Their investigation had uncovered the fact that the Fortress of Meropide has a "forbidden zone", the existence of which was confirmed by the guards. Lyney encouraged the Traveler and Paimon to go to the Coupon Cafeteria to get something to eat, assuring them that he would use his cards to get in touch with them again in the future. While in the cafeteria, the Traveler and Paimon met a man named Vidoc, who told them about the Fortress's "hidden rules," and how if you broke one, you might encounter something even worse than death. When the Traveler couldn't afford any more information, Vidoc left, telling them he would wait around the Rag and Bone Shop to exchange more information about the "hidden rules" for Credit Coupons. The Traveler and Paimon headed back to the dormitories to get some rest, but when the Traveler fell asleep, a Hydro Vision appeared in their dream. They saw visions of Childe in the Fortress of Meropide, saying, _"I hear... someone calling me..."_

**The Proscribed, Hidden in Plain Sight**
-----------------------------------------
The following day, the Traveler shared with Paimon the dream they had, where they were seeing as if through Childe's perspective. Paimon thought maybe the Vision that the Traveler possessed connected Childe's consciousness to the Traveler's, which gave them the idea that they might be able to use it to see everything the Harbinger experienced from his point of view.

![Image 1261: Ornate, steampunk-styled setting featuring golden lanterns and intricate piping](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/11/14/237301566/fb1349082aec5e47fb71d3de190fdfd4_4309849909049192548.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

In the meantime, they continued exploring the Fortress and met a man named Rowan, who had been working in the Fortress for almost 15 years. According to him, if the Traveler and Paimon kept working as they were, they might be putting themselves in danger. A "hidden rule" of the Production Zone was that if you work continuously for three days, then something bad will happen during lunch on the third day. Legends say that there was a worker who worked hard, both efficient and eager on the job, and that most other workers couldn't hold a candle to him. One time, he tried to test his limits and worked as long as he could. Then, during lunch on the third day, he disappeared into thin air, as if he'd evaporated. People asked some of his past friends about him, but they claimed they had never heard of the guy.

![Image 1262: Interior shot of a room with brick walls, stone floors, and a large metal door with intricate engravings, furnished with a bed, a table with books, and a small stool](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/11/14/237301566/fc2a33f9351c6c32fbb9f97f681429c5_4640599749335615829.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

In order to investigate the reports about the "hidden rules," the Traveler and Paimon decided to apply to work for three consecutive days. When lunchtime came on the third day, they headed to the cafeteria where they were served strange meat for lunch. The Traveler and Paimon asked the Coupon Cafeteria Supervisor, Wolsey, about the strange meal, but he felt it looked perfectly fine. They went to discuss it with Rowan, who they found at the infirmary. There they uncovered another rumor, saying that there's never anybody in the infirmary in the half hour before lunch, and nobody knows where Sigewinne, the head nurse, goes during that time. They later found Sigewinne at the Production Zone, who said she leaves the infirmary a half hour before lunch because usually everyone is busy around that time and there are no patients to look after.

![Image 1263: An indoor photo of a mysterious looking vault with lanterns and pillars with engraved ancient texts](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/11/14/237301566/c37c2a48cefbc06cf02cdea0cce06b72_7042556434324322830.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

As they continued exploring, the Traveler and Paimon visited the Pankration Ring, where they learned of another "hidden rule" — if you buy both boxers' tickets and support them both, something bad will happen the next morning. In order to investigate, the Traveler bought tickets for both fighters. The next morning, they received an unexpected package with a small bottle that contained red liquid. They discussed the contents of the strange package with Collins, who told them of the "hidden rule," and during the conversation, he revealed the tournaments make so little that even the current tournaments can only be held thanks to funding from the producer of Fonta. Information scattered around the ring showed that without assistance from the Fontaine Research Institute, development of the new product was slow, and some researchers on the project have voiced concerns. They had no choice but to let the new product undergo the first phase of promotional trials without a designated name or packaging. They decided to only conduct closed, small-scale trials for the time being. They also ran into a promoter for Fonta Co., who was responsible for promoting their drink products.
With their findings for the day gathered, the Traveler realized that their discoveries were not helping them find out where Childe went, and they decided to take a break.

**Lost in Deep Seas**
---------------------
Having obtained enough coupons, the Traveler and Paimon approached Vidoc to inquire about the "hidden rules." He warned them to steer clear of the pipes that make strange sounds late at night, for even if they managed to avoid the guards, they might find something even more terrible there, such as a group of cannibals. Vidoc went on to say that every month, the cannibals would meet a few times in the dead of night. Rumor has it that they might be connected to the people that have disappeared.

Due to their curiosity, the Traveler and Paimon planned to investigate the new "hidden rule" after having lunch, but Vidoc was nowhere to be found. Seeking an alternative approach, they asked a guard if he had ever encountered anything odd during his nighttime patrols. They told him they heard strange noises at night that disrupted their sleep. The guard revealed that these disturbances coincide with monthly pipe-cleaning sessions, with the next scheduled cleaning happening that very night. They returned to their dormitory to rest, and while there, the Traveler experienced a vision of Childe and realized he used the pipes to escape. The Traveler decided to investigate them that night.

Following the path, they encountered three individuals, who admitted that the "hidden rules" were fabricated to help Childe escape. The 3 "cannibals" were impressed by Tartaglia's strength and chose to follow him. Childe had left abruptly through the pipes and claimed to have heard a mysterious "voice." The route Childe took wasn't actually an exit but led to an abandoned factory area, and even if there were a way to escape from there into the sea, it would still be too deep. The "cannibals" took the Traveler and Paimon to the pipe's exit and on their approach, the exit was submerged in water. Armed with this newfound knowledge, the Traveler decided to enlist Freminet's help through Lyney as Freminet was an excellent diver.

**Cataclysm's Quickening**
==========================
**Into the Deepwater Murk**
---------------------------
The monthly "free day" came at the Fortress of Meropide, when all the prisoners were freed from work, and Lyney, the Traveler, and Paimon decided to continue their investigation. The Traveler and Paimon came across the "Bombshell Bros," Cuistot and Laverune. The brothers asked to pay for the "bombshell" information, and Laverune hinted at complimenting the free meals his brother prepared. After the compliment, Cuistot talked about the complex power structure of the Fortress. In the underwater world, only one person should not be crossed, Duke Wriothesley. The Duke had once been a prisoner of the Fortress and knew much more than he let on. If he did not care about something, he completely ignored it. Still, those, whom the Duke honored with attention were given all sorts of privileges, including special treatment in the infirmary. A talented researcher from the Fontaine Institute, Jurieu, often visited the infirmary along with another researcher, Lourvine, with whom he would get into fights. The two visited the infirmary so often that it began to be doubted whether it was their secret rendezvous.

![Image 1294: Interior of a room with beds, a desk with books, and an abstract figure standing near a small chair, all illuminated by warm light](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/12/20/237301566/fc2a33f9351c6c32fbb9f97f681429c5_6355679227548042344.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

After talking with the other prisoners, the Traveler and Paimon met with Lyney and shared the progress of their investigation. Freminet's journey along Childe's route was supposed to take about nine days, during which time the Traveler and Paimon were supposed to infiltrate the infirmary and find out if it was connected to the Fortress's forbidden zone. Not to arouse suspicion, they staged a scene where the Traveler became ill as if they had been poisoned and were rushed to the infirmary. Inside, they encountered Jurieu and Lourvine, who were arguing again. Looking around the infirmary, the Traveler saw only documents and boxes, but one block on the floor caught their attention as if it might have been moved. After receiving pills and recommendations from the head nurse of the Fortress, the Traveler and Paimon returned to the dormitories.
Sigewinne, who has special Melusine abilities, had already realized that her conversation with Lourvine and Jurieu in the infirmary was being overheard, so when Paimon and the Traveler appeared at the door, all three suddenly fell silent. Although she immediately realized that the Traveler was fine, she played along with them.

**The Truth Shrouded in Shadow**
--------------------------------
As planned, Freminet was given the job of cleaning the pipes and left the Fortress, while Lynette, feigning illness, entered the infirmary for further investigation. When the head nurse, Sigewinne, as was her custom, was to leave the infirmary half an hour before lunch, Lyney went to the infirmary to check on the progress of his sister's investigation. As expected, Sigewinne was not inside, but there was no sign of Lynette as well. According to the agreement with her brother, she was to warn about any deviation from the plan, so he suspected that something bad had happened. The Traveler, Paimon, and Lyney examined the strange sliding block on the floor but were unable to open it. Suddenly, they noticed a piece of paper on the floor, which read: _"Out of respect for your usual practices, I'll use a piece of paper or card as the medium to pass on my message. You may consider this as me giving you my best regards."_ On the other side was a message from the Duke: _"Would you care to guess where Miss Lynette of the Fatui could be right now?"_

Lyney was afraid that Wriothesley had known about the children from the House of Hearth's plans from the beginning, so he did not interfere with their investigation and then deceived them into a trap. He was sure that the Duke had deliberately made Freminet and Lynette disappear in order to challenge him. Blaming himself for what had happened, Lyney rushed to Wriothesley's office and attacked the Duke with accusations of kidnapping his sister and brother. He believed that the Duke had intentionally allowed Childe to escape from prison to get rid of the Fatui who had infiltrated the Fortress. And after the Harbinger disappeared, he spread the word to have The Knave send the children from the House of Hearth. In truth, Wriothesley had not planned to kidnap anyone. Lynette should have been enjoying the Fortress' finest tea, and the Duke had closed the gates of the Fortress behind Freminet to prevent him from returning. The manager of the Fortress had been following Fatui since before they entered the Fortress, and had no plans to interfere until they began investigating the "forbidden zone." In exchange for Lynette and Freminet's return, Wriothesley asked Lyney to arrange a meeting with the head of the House of Hearth, but the latter refused.

![Image 1312: Lyney is holding a playing card, looking up at Wriothesley, in Genshin Impact](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/12/20/237301566/f157e588381c2e24b0b2c20a0f8ec65e_6787146070643852697.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

To save the Fatui, the Traveler agreed to answer Wriothesley's questions about the hidden rules and the secret of the head nurse and her patients. The Traveler and Paimon had studied all the clues related to the hidden rules of the Fortress, so they easily answered the questions, but they did not know Sigewinne's secret. Losing patience, Lyney wanted to pounce on the Duke but was stopped by a calming dart from the head nurse who just arrived. Suddenly, the door of the office swung open, and the Champion Duelist, Clorinde, appeared on the threshold, along with an exhausted Freminet. When the diver set off along Childe's path, he found that the trail had disappeared. The concentration of water from the Primordial Sea outside the Fortress of Meropide increased, and Freminet, sensing this, tried to go back, but swallowed too much water and lost consciousness. Clorinde made it in time, and the boy got off with only minor symptoms. However, Sigewinne still demanded that he be taken to the infirmary for examination.

**Secret Keepers and Forbidden Zones**
--------------------------------------
When the children from the House of Hearth first infiltrated the Fortress, the Duke immediately suspected ill intentions but decided to observe them. He was interested in the circumstances of Childe's disappearance himself, so he allowed the Fatui to conduct their own investigation but soon realized that The Knave sent her charges for other reasons. Wriothesley decided to intervene so as not to drag the Fortress of Meropide into trouble. Knowing that the water outside the Fortress had changed, he hired the Champion Duelist to work independently and save Freminet.

![Image 1334: A dim, large room is lit by gold accents, including a large door with a cross in its center](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/12/20/237301566/399b775edc930c1479685ea47dc886e3_9129761752905836284.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

When the rumors of a "forbidden zone" turned out to be true, the Traveler and Paimon wanted to know the truth. On the floor of the Duke's office, there was a secret passage down where three huge isolation doors were hidden. Behind the doors was a spacious, completely empty room, in the middle of which a device similar to a massive sluice gate was installed. As soon as Wriothesley became the manager of the Fortress, he tried to find out what was behind the gates. The readings on the dashboard had not changed since he had taken up his post, but in the last year, the needle had crept upwards from its original position. Wriothesley sent researchers to study the changes in pressure and temperature of the water outside, but the readings remained unchanged. It had occurred to him later that the parameter might be related to the water of the Primordial Sea, and the situation with Freminet only confirmed his suspicions. The Primordial Sea was located directly below the sluice gate, and for some reason, the water level had suddenly begun to rise. Although the gate was still in place, all the indicators were already glowing red and some of the Primordial Seawater had flown out and seeped into the sea. If the situation continued, the device would no longer be able to contain the pressure of the Primordial Sea, the Fortress would be flooded, and all the people would turn into puddles of water.

![Image 1335: The architecture of a steampunk ship or building is shown in a low light shot](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/12/20/237301566/c9826c43df3a62db1d93cd3312c6139c_1125099657967051343.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

In addition to the sluice gates, the forbidden zone had a passage to the production zone, where Wriothesley was building a huge flying ship, "the Wingalet." The ship was inspired by the legend of the God King Remus, who descended upon the lands of Fontaine on the golden ship Fortuna. Jurieu and Lourvine were assigned to lead the project and were tasked with keeping the plan a secret. If the prisoners learned of the reason for the ship's construction, unrest would destroy the Fortress before the real disaster occurred, and the Fortress's manager could not allow this to happen. Knowing that the Traveler and Paimon would want to share the information with the Fatui, Wriothesley left it to them to decide.
