**Calamitous Tread**
--------------------
While Lyney was in the infirmary with Freminet and Lynette, he realized that the Primordial Sea was located directly below the Fortress of Meropide, but still had questions about the goals of the Fortress's manager. After making a choice, the Traveler and Paimon told their friends the information they had received from Wriothesley. Realizing the seriousness of the situation, Lyney agreed to talk to The Knave, as the Duke had requested.

![Image 1349: A steampunk-style illustration of a circular mechanism with pipes and ornate details](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/12/20/237301566/ad95fa0d2a04c94b33c3ebc32893efe8_8197980906514951112.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

When the Traveler and Paimon returned to the dormitories after a delicious dinner hosted by Sigewinne, screams suddenly rang out. Wriothesley had ordered everyone to evacuate the Fortress due to an incident on the lower levels, and the Traveler and Paimon rushed into the forbidden zone to meet with the Duke. The concentration of the Primordial Sea's water had reached a critical point, and the gate had ceased to hold back the flow. Wriothesley and Clorinde managed to stop the flow for a while by sealing and freezing the isolation doors, but they would not last long. Wriothesley sent the Traveler to Neuvillette for help, remaining the last line of defense at the doors.

![Image 1350: Arlecchino from Genshin Impact is overlooking Furina, who is playing with a black and white cat](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/12/20/237301566/62bded22b28987a673e36d29afe5a7ac_9083086254800799611.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

On their way to the opera house, they met the worried Chief Justice, who asked them to protect Furina during her meeting with The Knave. During tea, the tremors from the Primordial Sea were already felt on the surface, so Arlecchino dropped her feigned friendliness and accused Furina of inaction. While the Hydro Archon sat idly by, drinking tea and eating cake, the prophecy hung above the Fontainians' necks like a guillotine. The orphans of the House of the Hearth had devoted everything to save their homeland, but the Archon, as the Harbinger thought, did nothing. 

![Image 1351: Furina, a playable character of Genshin Impact, is sitting on the ground with a mysterious figure standing behind her and a cat running towards her](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/12/20/237301566/d408fb56d1b1a3d6df2417bc43c2d454_6125187007643236483.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

When The Knave asked about the measures taken to prevent the disaster and the goals of the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale, Furina was unable to answer. After finishing their tea, Arlecchino asked the Traveler and Paimon to accompany her to thank her for helping the children of the House of the Hearth. Shortly before Childe's disappearance, The Knave had attacked the Hydro Archon to find out where Fontaine's Gnosis was. When she saw the fear in Furina's eyes a second before the attack, she suspected that Neuvillette was the real Archon who possessed the Gnosis. When Arlecchino heard about another Harbinger's disappearance, she decided to use the situation to exert political pressure on the Chief Justice and Furina, and after several meetings with them, she realized that neither Neuvillette nor Furina was an Archon. At the end of the conversation, the Harbinger offered the Traveler her cooperation in rescuing Fontaine.

![Image 1352: Woman in a blue dress stands in front of a burst of light](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/12/20/237301566/8e713a362de4529d26568515115f6d53_5128783484949410402.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

When Neuvillette arrived at the Fortress of Meropide, he summoned his power to cause the waters of the Primordial Sea to recede and placed a new seal on the gate. Although the flow was stopped and the Fortress was saved, no one knew how long this calm would last.

_"A day may come when the prophecy is fulfilled,

And the waters burst forth…

But it’s not this day.

This ancient power could easily obliterate an entire race…_

_The tsunami of fury would unleash endless catastrophe._
_This sentence is too severe,_

_Forgive me for overruling it."_

Upon meeting Neuvillette, the Traveler realized that only one being could wield the power to push back the Primordial Sea — the Hydro Dragon. But even with his power, he did not have the full authority to deal with the prophecy. Neuvillette could only achieve victory over the Primordial Sea if the Archon disappeared and returned all of her elemental power to him. Until then, it was worth looking for another way to prevent the predicted catastrophe.

============================
**Deluge of Wrathful Waters**
-----------------------------
Some time had passed since the incident at the Fortress of Meropide, and the day had come for the Traveler and Paimon to leave the prison. A strong tremor suddenly shook the ground as they were filling out the release papers. The vibrations did not come from the bottom of the sea, but from the surface, so the Traveler hurried to Neuvillette. The Chief Justice had just received a report of the incident in the Belleau Region. The source of the vibrations was located in Poisson. After the shaking stopped, the water level in Poisson rose to frightening levels but soon returned to normal.

To find out what had happened, the Traveler and Paimon went to their friend Navia, the head of Spina di Rosula. In the village, they saw empty streets and many destroyed buildings. When people heard a loud noise, they first thought there was an explosion on the aquabus line, but water the color of the Primordial Seawater began to flow everywhere. Not everyone recognized the danger, and everyone on the street who happened to be close to the water didn't have a chance to escape. Those who realized what was happening started fleeing in a panic, desperately trying to get to higher ground. Many were injured in the stampede, and some fell from significant heights. Spina di Rosula quickly initiated a rescue operation, but there were many casualties. Fortunately, the water soon began to recede, and the panic subsided. The injured were given first aid and a preliminary count of the missing residents was conducted. Among the dead were Navia's assistants, Silver and Melus. They helped with the evacuation of residents and were unable to leave in time when they were swallowed up by the sea.

![Image 1386: Retro black and white shot of Mona being flanked by two suited characters wearing hats](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/12/28/237301566/915358d35c5c139c3755ea98f523c987_3096674014772888644.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

After going to the cemetery together with the Traveler and Paimon to see her father, Navia could not hold back her tears. She felt guilty for suggesting an evacuation plan in which Silver and Melus died. Although they were not afraid of death, they were the only family the woman had left. In life, they wanted to be buried with the grave of Navia's father, Callas, the former president of Spina di Rosula, but now she could not even bury them. At the cemetery, Navia, the Traveler, and Paimon were approached by the Fatui Harbinger, Arlecchino, whose people had been helping Poisson with the evacuation. The Fatui had been monitoring the water levels and keeping records for a long time and had also prepared a large number of emergency supplies, so it was thanks to their support that Spina di Rosula was able to quickly organize the rescue work. In addition, while gathering information, a child from the House of the Hearth discovered ancient ruins in the vicinity of Poisson. Judging by the dating of the ruins, they could be related to the prophecy and the coming disaster. As the situation became increasingly tense, Arlecchino asked the Traveler and Paimon to investigate these ruins. Navia couldn't stay away and wanted to distract herself from her thoughts and the dead, so she went with the Traveler.

**Meeting Is Also Parting**
---------------------------
![Image 1410: Jean Gunnhildr in the game Genshin Impact is dressed in a black hat and black gloves, as well as a blue and yellow outfit](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/12/28/237301566/6e41dddcec930f8d0d936969d233f826_7501240371624595185.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

A part of the ruins was flooded by the waters of the Primordial Sea, so Navia could not go any further. However, due to the terrain, she could not return either. As the Traveler, Paimon, and Navia crossed the crumbling bridge, the stones beneath Navia's feet suddenly collapsed, and she fell. The Traveler rushed to help her, but it was too late.

After falling into the Primordial Sea, Navia found herself in Poisson, where she was surrounded by people from the list of the dead. One of the girls asked her about an important trial, and Navia appeared in the courtroom. Since the head of Spina di Rosula had helped so many people in Poisson, she became one with them. This large family could not lose their heads, so they organized a trial to find Navia guilty, and she stayed with them. When she agreed to stay with the people in Poisson, Silver and Melus stood up for her. Although the woman had lent a helping hand to Poisson many times, she still remained an independent and separate person, whose free spirit could not be curbed by anything. During the trial, Navia suddenly realized that all the people in the opera house were dead, and all of them had turned into Oceanids before her eyes. Suddenly, the Chief Justice appeared in the courtroom: _"The court will adjourn for the rest of the day — in this, I shall hear no objections from any unauthorized party. Please leave with me, Miss Navia, while there is still time."_ Although Navia did not want to leave Silver and Melus, she said goodbye to them and went with Neuvillette.

![Image 1411: A tower stands on a cliff overlooking a green and blue landscape](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2025/01/21/237301566/a4611b88389774e93d71776a96d0d05c_8734650376510857342.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

During the conversation with the Chief Justice, he and the Traveler agreed to meet later in Poisson. Upon arrival, Neuvillette met the Fatui and The Knave, who told him about the ruins. When the ruins collapsed, Neuvillette was nearby and saw Navia fall into the water. Another second, and the woman would have dissolved in the water, but suddenly two Oceanids prevented her from falling. It only lasted a few seconds, but gave Neuvillette time to catch her. Even in death, Melus and Silver continued to protect their Demoiselle.

While giving Navia some time to be alone, Iudex and the Traveler discovered stone slabs. Although there were four niches, one slab was missing, and on the wall was an inscription: _"Reason dictates that this nation be destroyed. I shall record the history of its future here in its past..."_ Three of the slabs corresponded to Fontaine's prophecy. On the second slab, a woman was kneeling and praying, looking at the island in the middle of the sky. Neuvillette recognized her as the previous Hydro Archon, Egeria. She addressed the island in the sky as if repenting of a sin. On the third slab, Furina was in the water, with people gathered around her; and on the fourth slab, all the people had dissolved into the water, and only the Hydro Archon remained crying on her throne. Looking at the images in chronological order, the sequence seemed broken. Fontaine, sinking under the water, should have preceded the third slab, where the Hydro Archon was submerged. Although additional information was supposed to be hidden in the images, it was impossible to decipher it without the first slab, so Neuvillette and the Traveler decided to ask Furina some questions the next day.

**Hunters, Prophets**
---------------------
When the Traveler and Paimon arrived at the Spina di Rosula headquarters in the Fleuve Cendre to rest, they met their old friend, the astrologer Mona Megistus. "The Steambird" from Fontaine sent her an invitation to participate in the forum and talk about the events predicted in the prophecy from an astrological point of view. The prophecy concerned the fate of all of Teyvat, so determining whether it was true or not was the same as predicting the fate of the entire world. Only a very powerful seer could make such a large-scale and powerful prophecy. To find out if the prophecy was true, Mona agreed to contact her mentor, the astrologer from the Hexenzirkel, Barbeloth.

The next morning, as agreed, the Traveler and Paimon went to Neuvillette and Furina and found them arguing. The Chief Justice wanted to know about the prophecy, the stone tablets in the ancient ruins, and the secret investigation of the Hydro Archon, but Furina did not answer. Realizing that Furina was hiding something but did not want to tell, the Iudex proposed to create conditions where she would have no choice since many people would only reveal the truth during a trial. And although this was cruel to Furina, preventing a catastrophe was more important.

![Image 1435: The characters are standing outside a laboratory where some experiments are being done](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/12/28/237301566/a88d1fb58b94ee4f298124b0d4280ae5_6414161177919986314.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

To discuss the plan, the Traveler gathered the Iudex, the Champion Duelist, Clorinde, Navia, and the children of the House of the Hearth in Poisson. First, they needed to create a network of traps to lure Lady Furina. Hunting traps consist of bait, a trigger, and a containment device, while especially dangerous prey requires a lethal implement. They decided to stage a performance at the opera house to force the Archon to escape. Burning with guilt, she would go to Poisson, which had been evacuated after the disaster. There, the Traveler would lure her into a huge box, which would be delivered directly to the Opera Epiclese along the tracks dug by the Fatui. And in the end, Furina would be judged.

Returning to the Fleuve Cendre after discussing the plan, the Traveler and Paimon suddenly saw a cup of tea and heard a familiar voice that the Traveler had heard before during the endless Sabzeruz Festival in Sumeru in their heads. The voice introduced itself as the witch N. and told of a prophecy.

_"I believe that you understand, right?_

_Some things are insignificant... but others, you must reach out to change._

_Ultimately, fate shall serve as your only guide no matter what will happen in Teyvat's future._

_All you need to do is to play your part."_

Feeling the inevitable approaching, the Traveler and Paimon went out to the Court of Fontaine for a walk. They saw a newspaper with a report about them from their friend Charlotte from "The Steambird." The journalist carefully collected all the information about their adventures in Fontaine and wrote an article "The Traveler's Trail: World-Walker." When they met Charlotte herself, Paimon asked her what she would do if the prophecy came true tomorrow and all of Fontaine went underwater. She answered that she would stay in the office and continue preparing for their interview, and then send the finished material to other countries to leave behind such an article. When Paimon asked Traveler the same question, they said that they would continue the journey and appreciate every second in this world.

In the morning, they received a message that a riot had occurred in the opera house: people had accused the Hydro Archon of inaction, and she had fled. Realizing that the traps had begun to work, the Traveler and Paimon set off for Poisson.

**Apocalypse**
--------------
When the Traveler and Paimon arrived in Poisson in search of Furina, they heard her crying alone and talking to herself:

_"Should I just give up? This is all... meaningless..._

_What was meant to happen did happen after all. Everyone's dead..._

_I'm sorry... I'm so sorry..._

_Give up, Furina. There's no point in holding out…"_

As they approached her, she pretended that the incident at the opera house that morning had merely spoiled her enjoyment of the performance, and she disappeared to teach people a lesson. Suddenly, Furina was noticed by other people who came for her, and Paimon suggested hiding in a secret room. While they were inside, a new earthquake began, which could herald a new catastrophe. Furina admitted that she has been tirelessly exploring the mystery of the prophecy for many centuries. She once had her people all over Teyvat who collected information for her. They tried many different ways to keep the sea level so that the water did not rise, but all efforts were useless. In the end, she realized that she could not fight the Heavenly Principles, and what was predicted in the prophecy would certainly come true. Giving up in this struggle did not mean defeat for her, but coming to terms with fate, and finally being free. When people began to die, she was ready to give up, but the incident in Poisson showed that she could not decide for the Fontainians whether to surrender or continue to resist fate.

During the conversation, the "secret room" ended up on the stage of the Opera Epiclese, since everything that happened was part of the plan. The people who caused chaos in the Opera this morning were Spina di Rosula's subordinates. They changed into plain clothes, and came to the opera house as regular audience members, waiting for the perfect opportunity to incite an insurrection against the Hydro Archon. The people's resentment against their Archon has been building, so only a spark was all they needed to turn smoldering anger into a flame. They knew that Furina would most likely flee the scene and head to Poisson. The second group that pursued Furina were also members of the Spina di Rosula, and their goal was to lead Furina into the Giant Magic Box that the Fatui transported from Poisson to the Erinnyes through a dug tunnel. Clorinde and Neuvillette's task was to gather a crowd, prepare a stage, and make sure that the Champion Duelist would be immediately ready for a fight. The Traveler should have given Furina one last chance to tell the truth, but she did not take it. The interview that the Traveler and Paimon had previously given to Charlotte laid out a clear sequence of all the events that had occurred since their arrival in Fontaine, which should have helped in the prosecution process. Thus, began the great trial of the Hydro Archon.

Lady Furina was accused of posing as an Archon and deceiving the people of Fontaine as a mere mortal. The prosecution demanded that Furina touch the water of the Primordial Sea. Since no one wanted to see another dissolution, in case of unforeseen circumstances, they took a weak solution of water and called Sigewinne, the Head Nurse from the Fortress of Meropide, to conduct an examination. Not knowing that there was only a solution in the bowl, Furina dared to touch the water, but Sigewinne's examination showed that the Archon had received the same skin changes as an ordinary mortal. As a result, the Chief Justice found Furina guilty, and the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale made the final verdict: _"The Hydro Archon, guilty to be punished via the death sentence."_

![Image 1463: Drawing on the wall showing a girl with a hooded cloak hovering over a man inside a bubble, with waves and crowds of people behind her and winged creatures at the bottom](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/12/28/237301566/b0fb20592e699cd5342b9c87d6fab121_3570589706562458181.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

When the verdict was delivered, Freminet appeared in the courtroom and found the fourth stone slab with the prophecy written on it. It showed the first Hydro Archon, Egeria, releasing her divine power turning the Oceanids into human beings. In the Fontaine of old, the previous Hydro Archon sensed the yearning of her Oceanid familiars for life on land. The Oceanids were enamored with the beauty and romanticism of human beings, and, wishing to have those experiences for themselves, expressed to the Hydro Archon their desire to become of a similar kind. However, even though water as an element is intricately linked with the power of life, the Hydro Archon, as one of The Seven, did not possess the authority to create a new form of human life. Not one to give in, she eventually found a way to create permanent human bodies for her familiars by appropriating the power of this planet's Primordial Sea. She poured Primordial Sea water into the Oceanids' blood vessels, creating humanoid mimics in the process. But if Fontainians were ever to come into direct contact with water from the Primordial Sea, the power within their bodies would escape these artificial restraints and return to the Sea. As a result, their forms would collapse, and they would be reverted to their original state as Oceanids. The Hydro Archon never received permission from the Heavenly Principles to create a new "human" race, and thus, she and all of her creations came to shoulder the original sin of "appropriating the power of the Primordial Sea." The Traveler and Paimon were mistaken in thinking that the third slab should be the last: the Fontainians carried out the trial of the Hydro Archon in it, which was happening at that moment. Each step in an attempt to avoid fulfilling the prophecy only helped to make it true.

![Image 1464: Enigmatic digital illustration featuring a crystalline jellyfish hovering over a tiered platform, bathed in hues of violet, indigo, and bright teal](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/12/28/237301566/15c68a65ed9aa49b3fe80085734d56d6_5707391307571992135.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

However, if everyone saw the main threat in the flood of the Primordial Sea, it turned out to be the All-Devouring Narwhal, which the Traveler saw through Tartaglia's Vision. During the trial, a rift suddenly opened in the courtroom, through which the narwhal and the Harbinger fighting with it entered. The monster did not belong to Teyvat and had traversed the stars, weeping all the while. It had been greedily consuming the energy from the planet's Primordial Sea, using it to grow. It was his actions that led to the rise of the sea level. Since the Fontainians had the Primordial Sea in their blood, they attracted the narwhal to themselves, and, leaving the waters of the Primordial Sea, it decided to head straight to the opera house, where so many Fontainians had gathered. The narwhal absorbed too much of the Primordial Sea's energy, and at that point, had become practically integrated with the Sea itself. Even if the entirety of Teyvat were to be destroyed, it could still survive, and swim off towards some other world. Tartaglia, who fought the monster for a long time, was able to gain time, and without him, the narwhal would have reached land much earlier. Thanks to the intervention of Neuvillette and Tartaglia, the Harbinger and the narwhal disappeared back into the rift, and those gathered in court began to come up with a new plan. The words of the witch N gave hope that even if the prophecy was fulfilled, they would have a chance of salvation.

**The Opera of Noirceur and Blancheur**
---------------------------------------
![Image 1488: Furina standing in front of a mirror, which shows her original appearance](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/12/28/237301566/6b63ba3a7d5c46b0a07282251614a445_2524516851391134543.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

After the incident, Neuvillette found himself in the consciousness of the Hydro Archon, and the Traveler saw Furina's past. The real Hydro Archon was Focalors, who was once Egeria's Oceanid familiar and was turned into a human. 500 years ago, the first Hydro Archon died in the Khaenri'ahn Cataclysm and chose Focalors as her successor to the Divine Throne. Egeria knew that the prophecy would come true and that the Heavenly Principles could not be resisted. She placed the solution to this problem on the shoulders of Focalors. Focalors pondered for a long time how to counter the prophecy and found the only possible answer: it was necessary to deceive the Heavenly Principles during the fulfillment of the prophecy. After becoming an Archon, Focalors separated her newfound divinity from her body and spirit. The human counterpart she left behind, she named "Furina." After she made Furina, she also cursed her, so as long as Focalors's divinity continued to exist, Furina could not die to fulfill the prophecy. Furina was tasked to forever play the part of the god from the prophecy to create a deceitful appearance of that prophecy coming to pass. Focalors promised that Furina's torture would eventually end in a magnificent and dramatic trial, and everyone would be saved. Furina didn't know when the final trial would be, so for all these five hundred years she played her role, trying to solve the prophecy and save the people. She had to have a lot of pain and suffering, but for the sake of saving all the Fontainians, she was ready to endure it.
When Furina first took accession, she initially wanted to seem like a generous and caring god, but people considered her behavior as a weakness. Then Furina decided to become what people imagined: strong, significant, brave, and confident.

_"May law be the prayer on our lips._

_May judgment be our worship. Let us light the fires, and drink to the future of Fontaine!_

_There is no trouble in this world that justice cannot solve._

_All that is needed is for you, my people, to believe in it, heart and soul."_

For many years, Furina played her role: she participated in court sessions, received residents, and all this time she did not stop waiting for the trial that would solve everything and trying to fight the prophecy. Researchers conducted hydrological studies and tried to find a way to stop the sea level, but no one could find a solution.

182,375 "scenes"500 years

later, Furina had almost no strength left to perform this play, but she could not give up for the sake of the people of Fontaine and Focalors. When the Traveler asked her to tell the truth in the Magic Box, Furina wanted to speak out and think about herself at least once, but she never did.

![Image 1489: A bright blue anchor floats in the sky, inside an enclosed space](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/12/28/237301566/fe8ba9a40189f58b336318caf2724502_5231398309600782488.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

While Furina ruled Fontaine, Focalors accumulated energy to deceive the Heavenly Principles. She created and placed her divinity along with the Hydro Gnosis in the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale. The Oratrice converted the people's faith in justice into Indemnitium, a type of energy that powered Fontaine. Although it was used for trials, its main purpose was to kill the God of Justice along with the Divine Throne when the time came. Focalors understood that only power of this magnitude could hope to destroy the Hydro Archon's Throne. The destruction of it meant the return of the stolen power to the Hydro Dragon Sovereign, Neuvillette, whom Focalors entrusted to judge the Fontainians. As Focalors bid farewell to the Chief Justice, the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale carried out the sentence, destroying the throne of the Hydro Archon, killing Focalors, and returning full authority to the Dragon Sovereign.

![Image 1490: Anime girl with white hair and red eyes holding a purple orb](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/12/28/237301566/48f8d3d0c77024fa11df66f6e29cfe40_4981431024177322093.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

With full authority over Hydro, Neuvillette gained enough power to defeat the All-Devouring Narwhal and separate it from the Primordial Sea. Together with the Traveler, they entered the Primordial Sea, where they fought with the All-Devouring Narwhal and met Tartaglia's master, Skirk. She revealed that the monster was the pet of her master,

Surtalogi,The Foul

one of the five Sinners of Khaenri'ah. During the fight with the narwhal, energy from the Primordial Sea came to the surface and the prophecy unfolded in full force.

![Image 1491: A gigantic flying machine with architecture including domes, a clock, gears, and jets flies low to the water, with a fog-like shroud covering its lower half and the water around it](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/12/28/237301566/30e52c0f12e3a9272267dce7b8a66666_3734531003202747129.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

As predicted, all of Fontaine drowned in the water, leaving only Furina weeping on her throne. Thanks to the efforts of Fatui, Spina di Rosula, and the flying ship "Wingalet," built by the Duke of the Fortress of Meropide, the Fontainians were saved. Finally, the water receded without dissolving anyone.

**Finale**
----------
After experiencing the flood, the Fontainians began to restore the destruction. "The Steambird" journalist, Charlotte, interviewed Navia about how Champion Duelist Clorinde and the "friendly neighbors," Fatui, helped Spina di Rosula restore Poisson. At the Fortress of Meropide, researchers Lourvine and Jourie, who created the "Wingalet," also became part of Charlotte's report, as did the children of the House of the Hearth: Lyney, Lynette, and Freminet, who were again distributing the Magic Pockets. They said that the Fatui Harbinger Arlecchino received the Gnosis from Neuvillette, and Tartaglia returned to Snezhnaya to recover from his wounds.

![Image 1507: A person with long white and blue hair standing in front of a city](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/12/28/237301566/2e4606d4887212e132b884a7025ddfae_4723262396360575419.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

When Traveler and Paimon finished the interview, they returned to Neuvillette, who recounted what had happened in the courtroom. Since he gained complete control over the Hydro element, he used the ancient dragons' authority to grant the Fontainians true "blood," after the fashion in which life was first brought into being on this planet. After this, the Fontainians became ordinary people who couldn't be dissolved by the water of the Primordial Sea. In addition, he forgave them of their original sin.

When the Traveler and Paimon went to the surface during the fulfillment of the prophecy, Neuvillette stayed with Skirk, and she revealed that the Gnosis the Chief Justice had with him was the remains of the third Descender and only brought misfortune with it. That is why Neuvillette so easily parted with the Gnosis, which was useless to him, and gave it to Arlecchino.
After Focalors's death and the destruction of the Oratrice, Neuvillette became the ruler of all of Fontaine and was left alone to make decisions during the trial. Furina found her mortality and finally became free.

**The First Era**
=================
According to legend, many millennia ago, the eternal throne of the heavens came to Teyvat, and the world was made anew. The true lord, the Primordial One, fought with the dragon-lords of the old world. After forty years, the seven rulers were defeated, and the seven nations submitted to the heavens. The great sovereign, the Primordial One, began the creation of heaven and earth for the sake of humans — their creations, whom they cherished most and who were soon destined to appear upon this earth. For four hundred years, the Primordial One and their four shades created mountains, rivers, birds, animals, fish, grass, trees, and finally — people. From that time on, people made a covenant with the Primordial One and entered a new age. The lands that would become Fontaine in the Great Terrestrial Lake were called Meropis.

Legend has it that

the first of the oceans Primordial Sea

had a composition similar to that of blood and that life within it was not individual. To set foot upon land or take to the skies, life evolved blood vessels to keep that primordial ocean flowing within itself. The beating heart that commanded this Primordial Sea of blood was the first Hydro Dragon. Each time that heart pulsed, all life would arise and give it praise. When that first heart was removed during the war with the Primordial One, the envoy of Celestia, the leader upon whose shoulders rested the duty to create life, came to the great primeval sea, and there she made another heart, Egeria. That heart had like nobility unto a dragon, but lacked its outer form, and had the majesty of a god, yet was

bereft of any divine duty.not yet an Archon

And though it was created by a ruler of humans, its substance and essence were composed entirely of original matter from this world, with no outside elements. She was the tears that flowed into the primordial sea, seeking communication and understanding, a pursuit that caused her to weep. And it was due to this compassion that she committed all the sins that all beings of pure water must beware of.

![Image 2060: Watery graphic with a white and blue crystalline shape in the center, surrounded by ripples, yellow flowers, and orange petal-like shapes on a blue background](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2025/02/03/237301566/51a3150adb1422d67f2fc3f9ef37e9a9_5058258962982324173.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

Egeria created the

Oceanids,Lochfolks

elemental lifeforms. The Oceanids, admiring the lives of humans, also wanted to become them. Using the power of the Primordial Sea, Egeria turned some Oceanids into humans whose blood flowed with the Primordial Seawater. This creation of people became the original sin of Egeria. Celestia was angry with Egeria for stealing the power of the Sea, so they imprisoned her. Thus, the prophecy of the future Fontaine was born:
_"Every person in Fontaine is born with 'sin.' No matter how the Nation of Justice holds trial after trial, this sin cannot be absolved._

_Until one day, the water levels in Fontaine will rise, and the sinful people will slowly be drowned..._

_In the end, the people will all be dissolved into the waters, and only the Hydro Archon will remain, weeping on her throne... Only then will the sins of the people of Fontaine be washed away."_

Legend has it that in the first era, the earliest peoples were self-supporting in their virtue, needing no laws or authorities. The envoys of the

heavenly city Celestia

walked the earth, and with their guidance, the people enjoyed enduring peace, prosperity, and abundance from the ancient days. This Heaven-blessed reign lasted countless generations until people grew tired of their inscrutable eternity. Their offspring ceased to listen to the oracles. Instead, they desired things never promised to them by the divine, trying to break free from their fate. Enraged by their behavior, Heaven sent gigantic waves to smash the settlers' cities. A hundred days of rain came afterward, and the roaring tides drowned all sin and arrogance, and thus were the early peoples brought to an end. When the tide receded and the earth was revealed again, no cities nor civilizations now stood above the high waters. Survivors and the newborn alike lived amidst the forests and rivers, shorn of all knowledge and wisdom. Human lives were no different from those of wild animals on the earth or in the sea, driven by the laws of nature — muddling through time with neither beginning nor end.

**Remuria**
===========
![Image 2082: The Grand Narukami Shrine, with staircase leading up to the entrance, framed by towering structures and luminescent flora](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2025/01/18/237301566/4417194d9a22aa68cbc2c9d4aa037acd_7155415801148772578.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

While Egeria was imprisoned, a faraway god Remus refused to submit to

King Deshret Al-Ahmar

and arrived in Meropis from Sumeru. He chose the ancient ruins as his grave, and there he met one of Celestia's envoys, Sybilla, who had survived the great flood. Sybilla, a Golden Bee who could see the future, prophesied that Remus would create a prosperous state and bring civilization and justice to the people, but which would ultimately lead to their destruction. Knowing that fate could not be resisted, Remus agreed to take the first step along the predicted path but sought to alter the future of his empire. Together with the seer Sybilla, Remus descended to Meropis on the golden ship Fortuna, and prosperity and order returned to these lands. He taught people how to farm and raise crops on the land, and built temples and cities with giant rocks to house the people. Most importantly, it was he who spread the beauty of music and art, differentiating humans from all other living beings, and causing them to see themselves as masters of all things. Remus built a great tower in Meropis, gathering the scattered people to form a new nation.

![Image 2083: A glowing, ghostly sea creature glides above an underwater ruin featuring a partially sunken ship and rocky pillars covered in seaweed](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2025/01/18/237301566/d3c8cf022bac76a55f5125c200946e97_2339189456724358479.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

Remus could not accept that the predicted glory of Remuria would last only a century and, on the advice of Sybilla, traveled to the Primordial Sea, to the Fontemer — the kingdom where the Dragonborn dwelled. At that time, they were ruled by the Vishap-prince, Scylla. In the deepest depths of the waters, the domain of eternal night, he met Egeria, and she told him about how she committed an unforgivable sin and how an irrevocable punishment fell upon her. In the end, Remus decided to take the Pure Grail with him on his journey and promised Egeria he would create a world free from the shackles of providence. Scylla followed him to ensure that the promise was fulfilled.

In an attempt to escape fate, Remus created stone bodies for his people from the blood of insoluble Ichor, so that time could not destroy them. He created a great melody so that every free person would control their own destiny. To bring civilization to the northern "barbarians," the Harmosts of Remuria led armies of golems to conquer the peoples of the High Sea, but the followers of Egeria, known as the Lochknights, refused to submit. They swore to protect

the spirits Oceanids

of the pure springs and other knights from the warriors of Remus. Their main goal was to find the Pure Grail to wash away their sin and bring Egeria back.

![Image 2084: Golden harp with ornate decorations, blue column, and pink strings on a black background](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2025/01/18/237301566/bb04749691763bf91c08ae162788a488_7682766630834679249.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

To free his subjects from the tyranny of fate, Remus united all the souls, thoughts, and desires of the Remurians in a great Symphony, Phobos, that was meant to last for thousands of years. To master the "Symphony" was to master fate itself. Remus infused this melody into Ichor, hoping people could control their destiny by playing this music. But the Symphony led to the fall of the empire. Gradually, the Remurians became slaves to Phobos and followed not their desires, but rather the will of the great Symphony. The power the Remurians gained led to violence, destruction, and hatred, and so Remus decided to destroy Phobos. He created his last symphony, Requiem, which was an order for the Phobos to self-destruct, and entrusted it to his friend Scylla, the Prince of the Vishaps of the Fontemer. Phobos learned of Remus's plan and, possessing the body of one of Remuria's Harmosts, chained up Scylla. He failed to make it to the capital in time, so when Remus sacrificed himself to release the power of the symphony, it went out of control and Remuria sank.

Although the Remurians brought death and destruction to the High Sea, they remain forever in the history of Fontaine. The Remurian civilization deeply influences Fontainian music, drawing, architecture, and sculpture. Echoes of the Golden Empire can be seen in almost every building in Fontaine. It is believed that Remurians are the font of all the arts in Fontaine. Thus, the Musicians' Association highly values the scores written by Boethius, especially his work "The Flying Outlander."

**Egeria's Return**
===================
An ancient legend says that in the years when the Mistress of Many Waters was imprisoned and God King Remus ruled the lands, pure spring water had to be hidden away in concealed mountain streams, and the Lochknights were born in these sanctuaries. The knights swore by armor of silver to protect the Oceanids and to protect other knights who also kept faith in the Mistress of Many Waters, resisting the omnipresent golden power that blotted out the sky and outshone the sun. They swore never to draw their sword against those who pledge faith in Egeria and to never compromise in the face of evil. They opposed the omnipresent golden authority with nothing but their frail bodies of flesh and bone.

One legend says that when sin tempted the City of Eternity to its fall, the Lochknights faced unimaginable trials and endured suffering never before known. But in the end, the people's heartfelt longing reached the heavens. Then, thanks to their pure hearts and the Pure Grail obtained through countless sacrifices, the Mistress of Many Waters was freed from her prison and restored. Another legend says that when sin tempted the City of Eternity to its fall, a singer named Erinnyes faced unimaginable trials and endured sufferings never before known. Yet, she was unable to find that Pure Grail. But it was the heavens who chose the Mistress of Many Waters, commanding her to return from her primeval prison to replace the golden king and rule the sea ruins. Whatever the legend may be, when Egeria returned from captivity, she was awarded a shard of that one who was first and gained both an Archon's right and the divine duty-come-lately. Thus Egeria's reign as Hydro Archon of Fontaine began.

**The Cataclysm**
=================
![Image 2127: A video game landscape featuring craggy rocks, flowers, and trees on a foggy, blue-toned hillside](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2025/01/18/237301566/177d683344212d7e080b86df098e748d_5376246021369506659.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

Five hundred years ago, the creatures of the Abyss flooded Teyvat, and all the forces of the people were directed toward defending their lands. Elynas appeared in Fontaine — a colossal being whose very existence poisoned the water and the land. Although Elynas realized that he only brought destruction and suffering and decided to die, the damage he caused was irreparable. The water was polluted, and the Oceanids could no longer live in Fontaine. In their place, tainted phantasms began to appear. Elynas's body was petrified and turned into an island in the Beryl Region.

![Image 2128: A serene meadow with a magical plant, reminiscent of a blue-white lotus with hints of purple, as the focal point](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2025/01/18/237301566/0058c3c9591f49bc0ac12760d5250fb4_2067961237939774552.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

Millennia ago, Nabu Malikata, the Lord of Flowers, created a "daughter," Khvarena, whose fate was inevitable death and sacrifice. When Nabu Malikata sacrificed herself, she asked her friend, Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, to take care of Khvarena. The Goddess of Wisdom turned Khvarena into the divine bird Simurgh, charging her with the protection of two worlds, with the guardianship of the border between new birth and death. When the Cataclysm came many years later, the leader of the realm of water, Egeria, was slain in the Vourukasha Oasis in a battle with the Abyss monsters, and her body was transformed into a sea of pure dew, known as the Amrita. Then, the Amrita was desecrated by the Abyss, but the bird Simurgh fulfilled its duty by drinking from the Amrita and scattering into many pieces. Rukkhadevata grew the Harvisptokhm tree from the Amrita with the sacred lotus Gaokerena inside. The lotus contained Egeria's consciousness, allowing her to maintain the barrier between the human world and the Abyss in the Tunigi Hollow.
Before her death, Egeria chose her successor, Focalors, who had previously been an Oceanid familiar. After the death of Egeria, many Oceanids lost contact with Fontaine. They did not recognize the new Hydro Archon and desired only to keep the dreams of yesteryear alive. Many Oceanids made pilgrimages across the sweltering Sumeru Desert to reach Harvisptokhm and see their goddess.

During the Cataclysm, waves crashed onto Fontaine, flooding the orphanage — the Narzissenkreuz Institute, the Institute of Natural Philosophy — Fontaine's main scientific institution at the time, and the first opera house. This is now called the "first diluvian period." In the "Song of Dobharcu," the writer describes the outcome of the war: the great Hunter's Ray known as the Stormlord stirred huge waves in its death throes, causing a flood. In reality, the Fontemer Aberrants are merely aquatic creatures, incapable of flooding half of Fontaine. Since the first diluvian period, the newly built Fontaine Research Institute has been preoccupied with the thought that there might be a second one. Some proposed recovering the ruins lost to the waves and building an underwater city, whereas others looked up to the untouchable sky islands overhead to build a metropolis in the clouds. A researcher Rene de Petrichor calculated the inevitability of the Second Flood, and to avoid another catastrophe, he founded an esoteric organization, the Narzissenkreuz Ordo.

**Prophecy**
============
Many years ago, one of the Khaenri'ahn Great Sinners, Vedrfolnir, known as "The Visionary," created stone tablets in Fontaine to document Egeria's original sin and the future of Fontaine. In this way, he wanted to record the history of Fontaine's future in the past. Egeria knew for certain that the prophecy would come true and that the Heavenly Principles could not be resisted. After her death, the burden of addressing this prophecy fell on Focalors.

Many organizations in Fontaine attempted to combat the prophecy. The Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering, founded by the great scientist Alain Guillotin, measured the level of the Primordial Sea and worked to transform the Court of Fontaine into a city in the sky that would remain safe from flooding. The radical organization, the Narzissenkreuz Ordo, created by Alain Guillotin's friends, Rene de Petrichor and Jakob Ingold, followed the path of the ancient Remurians. Just as the Remurians placed their souls in incorruptible stone bodies so that time could not destroy them, Rene de Petrichor wanted to separate the souls of the Fontainians to allow them to wait out the apocalypse and be reborn in a new world. Since contact with the water of the Primordial Sea reverted the Fontainians to their original forms as Oceanids, Rene and the Ordo dissolved people and used the power of the Abyss, obtained from the blood and flesh of the dead Elynas, to create Neohumans capable of surviving the prophecy. The experiments and dissolution of people led to the banning of the organization, and Rene went to the Primordial Sea to wait for the fulfillment of the prophecy.

![Image 2162: Two women from Genshin Impact are pictured, one with white hair in a white top and the other in a black outfit and hat, facing each other and in profile](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2025/01/18/237301566/7d385a6c1ba9e5d7ccb649d37c020ec0_2865294744126782736.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

Focalors herself pondered how to counter the prophecy for a long time and found the only possible answer: it was necessary to deceive the Heavenly Principles during the fulfillment of the prophecy. After becoming an Archon, Focalors separated her newfound divinity from her body and spirit. The human counterpart she left behind, she named "Furina." Furina was just a human, but she could feel joy, sorrow, and everything in between; she could be as vain and conceited, or as meek and vulnerable as she wished; her strengths were of a kind only a human could possess, as were her shortcomings. In Focalors's eyes, Furina's humanity was what made her perfect, the person Focalors always wanted to be. After she made Furina, she also cursed her, so that as long as Focalors's divinity continued to exist, Furina could not die to fulfill the prophecy. Furina was tasked to take the stage in the opera house, embrace the role of leading lady, and eternally play the part of the god foretold in the prophecy to create the illusion that the prophecy had come true. Focalors promised that her torture would eventually end in a magnificent and dramatic trial, and everyone would be saved. Furina didn't know when the final trial would be, so for all these 500 years she played her role, trying to solve the prophecy and save the people.
While Furina ruled Fontaine, Focalors accumulated energy to deceive the Heavenly Principles. She placed her divinity, along with the Hydro Gnosis, into the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale — a special device in the Opera Epiclese, where all trials were held. The Oratrice converted the people's faith in justice into Indemnitium, a type of energy that powers Fontaine. If this power, accrued over five centuries, had only been used to sustain Fontainians, it could have lasted for millennia, but it had another purpose. Along with the Chief Justice, this device passed sentences in court, and its sentence was always of paramount importance. Although it was used for trials, in truth its main purpose was to kill the God of Justice along with the Divine Throne when the time comes. Focalors understood that only power of this magnitude could hope to destroy the Hydro Archon's Divine Throne, shaking the rules established by Celestia and shattering the institution that is The Seven.

**Chief Justice**
=================
![Image 2188: A full shot illustration of a tall man wearing a navy outfit standing under a structure of swirling blue light](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2025/01/19/237301566/6ece63f5f6805280554d805e9ccaf9a8_3395546736253576286.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

Since Egeria was the heart of the Primordial Sea, while she was imprisoned in the land of dragons, the true Hydro Dragon Sovereign could not be reborn. After her release, the Hydro Dragon was born in the form of Neuvillette, a human. It is believed that the Serpent God, Orobashi, escaped to the Dark Sea, to Enkanomiya, during the Archon War. There, Orobashi conducted experiments on the Bathysmal Vishaps. As a result, the vishaps evolved and were able to master the power of other elements, losing their original purity. Therefore, the Dragon Sovereign could no longer be born among them. There is a riddle in Enkanomiya: what walks on four feet in the early morning, two feet during the day, and three feet at night? The answer is: A vishap who transforms into a person to attend a ball, then breaks one of its legs and eventually ends up walking with a cane. Although adults may think that there is a conspiracy here, because a vishap cannot transform into a human, according to an ancient prophecy, the ruler of the vishaps must certainly descend in the form of a human.

When Focalors became an Archon, Neuvillette was invited to the Court of Fontaine to serve as Iudex. Focalors knew that when the grand trial time came he could never again declare them to be "guilty." In the beginning, Neuvillette was uninterested in the humans' existence, but after five centuries alongside them, he became quite fascinated with the joys and sorrows of humanity and even attempted to feel as they feel.
Neuvillette brought the Melusines, an intelligent race that emerged from Elynas' body as a result of a powerful explosion that occurred during the battle between the Marechaussee Hunters and members of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo, to the Court of Fontaine. At first, people were unkind to the Melusines: they considered them creatures of disaster, and dangerous for people, so they threw stones at them and told them to return to their village. Some people were subconsciously wary of the Melusines because they looked different. A group of supporters of the old regime, whose interests were infringed as a result of Neuvillette's reform, decided to commit murder and blame Melusines for it. A Melusine agent of the Marechaussee Phantom chose to sacrifice herself in this situation, as she considered it the only way out. Thanks to her courage, the dream of living peacefully with people came true: today, four hundred years later, the Melusines are respected members of the Court of Fontaine.

**Fulfillment of the Prophecy**
===============================
![Image 2218: A man with long white hair decorated with blue streaks stands in a large hall, looking at a woman in a blue gown who is walking towards him](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2025/01/19/237301566/c892f91506e3c6d807953bcc10f06e06_3855565669394072359.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

Five hundred years after Furina became an Archon, the prophecy began to come true. The water of the Primordial Sea began to rise, dissolving the people. The water rose first in Poisson. The town's residents did not immediately recognize the danger, so passers-by who found themselves near the water immediately disappeared. After this, people began to run in panic, hoping to reach higher ground. Some were injured during the stampede, while others fell from great heights. The head of Spina di Rosula, Poisson's leading organization, with the support of the Fatui Harbinger, Arlecchino, was able to ensure the safety of the affected residents of Poisson, evacuating them from the town. The people of Fontaine accused Furina of inaction, marking the beginning of the final trial she had long awaited. Over the course of five centuries, Focalors accumulated enough Indemnitium, and the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale rendered its judgment: _"The Hydro Archon, guilty to be punished via the death sentence."_ Focalors met with the Dragon Sovereign, Neuvillette, to entrust him with the decision upon the people of Fontaine. When Focalors said goodbye to the Hydro Dragon, the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale carried out the sentence, destroying the Hydro Archon's throne, killing Focalors, and transferring absolute control over the Hydro element to Neuvillette. After gaining his full power, Neuvillette cleansed the Fontainians of their original sin and turned them into real people, saving them from the flood.

![Image 2219: Scene from a video game showing a blue creature floating over a tiered platform structure, and a character standing in front of a bright blue beam](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2025/01/19/237301566/15c68a65ed9aa49b3fe80085734d56d6_189253993784143385.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

Shortly before the prophecy began to come true, the Oratrice declared the Eleventh Fatui Harbinger, Tartaglia, guilty in the case of serial disappearances and dissolution of the people, a phenomenon that had plagued Fontaine for the past two decades. People saw this dissolution as a sign of the fulfillment of the prophecy, on par with the rising of the waters of the Primordial Sea, which caused Fontainians to dissolve. Although Childe wasn't the root cause of the disaster, the Oratrice saw him as a part of the whole scene: when Tartaglia was 14, he fell into a bottomless crack in the earth's surface. There, by chance, he awakened the All-Devouring Narwhal — a mysterious and gargantuan creature from another world that wanted to absorb the Primordial Sea and caused the flood promised by the prophecy. According to Neuvillette, this judgment could be passed due to the liability by association, or Focalors could have deliberately used Tartaglia to buy time on the assumption that the Narwhal could be held at bay.
Gaining full authority, Neuvillette was able to defeat the All-Devouring Narwhal. During their fight, a huge amount of energy was released, which led to the flooding of the Primordial Sea and the complete fulfillment of the prophecy. As predicted, all of Fontaine was drowned in water, and only Furina remained, crying on her throne. Thanks to the combined efforts of the people of Fontaine, everyone was saved. Finally, the waters receded without dissolving any of the people.

**Present Day**
===============
After the destruction of the Divine Throne and Furina's resignation as an Archon, Neuvillette became the ruler of Fontaine. In addition, after Focalors' death, the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale ceased to function, and the Chief Justice became the sole judge of all decisions. Although he knows he must do much as an Elemental Dragon, he must above all else continue to serve Fontaine as its Chief Justice, combining the duties of both the Sovereign of Hydro and the Iudex into one. Since Neuvillette had no use for the power of the Gnosis, he gave it to the Fatui Harbinger, Arlecchino, to avoid unnecessary conflict.

![Image 2241: Anime-style profile art of the Hydro Archon, Furina, with white hair, blue eyes, and dressed in blue, looking at a blue orb, in front of a white cloudscape](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2025/01/19/237301566/3c6afb427c6ef8a356be11255a56f366_5455761741274453652.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

After Focalors' death, Furina was freed from her curse and became an ordinary human. Although people blamed her for failing to prevent the prophecies, Furina could finally be herself and stop playing the lingering role of the Hydro Archon. When Neuvillette relayed Focalors' words to her, she merely replied that she was tired and needed to rest. Having said that, she then packed her things and moved out of the opera house. Now her wounds have begun to heal, and she is already thinking about returning to theatrical performances, if not as an actress, then as a director. Thus, she directed the film "The Two Musketeers," which received the main award at the film festival, and became a consultant for the production of the play "The Little Oceanid."

![Image 2242: Decorative fountain in a city park, set against a backdrop of green grass, evergreen trees, and mountains](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2025/01/19/237301566/9779a4d8709c1dca6b5b7821380802e8_5872017574079530759.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

Before the Fontainians became true humans, they had a tradition of coming to the Fountain of Lucine and asking for a healthy child by throwing coins into the water. Although it was just a custom for them, in reality, the Oceanids who were blessed within the spring water would later descend as new humans in the coming months. This ritual has become unnecessary now, but it remains a local custom.

During the fulfillment of the prophecy,

the Duke Wriothesley

of the Fortress of Meropide provided great assistance in the giant ship "The Wingalet." This ship was inspired by the legend of how the ruler of Remuria, Remus, descended on the golden ship "Fortuna." When Wriothesley suspected that the Fortress of Meropide was hiding a passage to the Primordial Sea, he recruited researchers from the Research Institute, Jurieu and Lourvine, and began building the ship. When the Prophecy of Fontaine came to fruition, the Duke deployed the gargantuan ship, The Wingalet, to help with rescue operations. Once the waters receded, the ship returned to the prison and was placed in storage, garnering significant media attention and intriguing several researchers.
Poisson, where the waters began to rise first, suffered the most damage. Although many residents died, Spina di Rosula, who was in charge of Poisson, with the support of Fatui, was able to save most of the residents. After the incident, the village gradually began to recover, and Spina di Rosula's president, Navia, promised compensation to all victims. Although the organization's financial situation left much to be desired, this promise helped to express the attitude towards what had happened, so that people could trust the organization again.

**Energy**
==========
More than five hundred years ago, at that time, when controllable Pneumousia annihilation reactions had not been developed, and when Meks was seen as nothing more than curiosities and indulgences, manual labor remained a necessity. Many of the tools used in factories and shipyards ran on fuel oil, an outdated energy source with low efficiency. The tool's long grip was a fuel storage compartment, so they had to be handled with extreme caution. The underground city of the Fleuve Cendre was built with such tools, including a chainsaw, a drill, and a special blade. And it was these same tools that became weapons in the hands of the people of the Fleuve Cendre during its cleaning. As society developed, fuel oil devices fell into disuse, and tools were banned.

After the first diluvian period during the Cataclysm, Fontaine needed to solve the energy crisis. The search for new energy sources became the main focus of research at the main scientific institution — the Institute of Natural Philosophy. Significant efforts were made to transport Primal Constructs to the Institute for thorough examination due to the noticeable technological gap between the Primal Constructs found in the ruins of Sumeru's desert, and the clockwork machines prevalent during this era. Two young prodigies of the Institute, Alain Guillotin and Rene de Petrichor, used the characteristics of Ousia and Pneuma to construct a new kinetic core which eventually led to the first controlled annihilation reaction. Pneuma and Ousia can be found in all living organisms, soil, water, and ley lines in Fontaine.

Since Pneumousia is inherently unstable and inaccessible to the general population, Indemnitium became the primary source of energy during the reign of the Focalors. This energy was produced by the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale, which collected people's faith in justice during court hearings and converted it into energy, which was then used throughout Fontaine. As the Oratrice's main goal was to destroy the Divine Throne with the immense power of Indemnitium, only a small portion of it was used to supply Fontaine.

After the Divine Throne was destroyed, the Oratrice stopped working, and the opera house could no longer produce Indemnitium. Since the Dragon Sovereign had not only gained complete control over Hydro but also control over Pneumousia, Fontaine once again returned to this type of energy, which had become more stable. Since Neuvillette must supply all of Fontaine with his power, he cannot leave it for long.

**Inventions**
==============
![Image 2291: Genshin Impact's Golden Clockwork Meka boss fight, as the pair dances with each other](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2025/01/19/237301566/6652cd2808a2f41f493ac5d24aeab69e_7028453270187602556.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

Fontaine is a technologically advanced nation. One of their most famous inventions is Meks, created by Alain Guillotin and later the Fontaine Research Institute he founded. They were originally clockwork but later began to use Pneumousia energy. Clockwork Meks based on annihilation energy normally produce their energy by utilizing repeaters composed of special crystals to refine ousia and pneuma from Fontaine's environment. But outside of Fontaine, they can use pre-prepared Energy Blocks to move over short distances for short periods. Some Meks are designed for underwater and land-based attacks. For example, the Deepwater Assault Mek was created after the attack of Elynas five hundred years ago. The revered White Armada that sailed upon the great terrestrial lake was completely destroyed in defense of the nation. The designer hoped that were such a thing to happen again, the clockwork meka would possess enough naval firepower to be the first line of defense, going before the soldiers and generals. Other Meks are used for reconnaissance, repair, and construction. One of them was used to build the famous tunnel through Poisson. One of the earliest Meks was the prototype 4ACV07, a thinking Kamera created by Alain Guillotin to protect his sister in the service of the Marechaussee Phantom. One of the most recent Meks was the Experimental Field Generator, created by Edwin Eastinghouse to lift the entire Court of Fontaine into the air and avoid a second flood. Many Meks now stand guard over the Court of Fontaine and belong to the Maison Gardiennage.
Another famous invention of the Fontainians is the Kamera and Film Kamera, created by director and member of the Daydream Club, Xavier. He made some improvements to the Kamera and turned it into a Film Kamera that is also capable of continuously projecting a string of photos, thus creating moving images. In addition to the Film Kamera, Xavier helped create the Mikage Furnace in Inazuma, a machine that can fully utilize the powers of the Tatarigami. When the furnace was damaged by saboteurs from the Sangonomiya troops, he installed a protective dome around it and helped restore it. In addition to Xavier, the club includes Garcia, the creator of the Numbering Machine, Félix Yogue, the inventor of the Evermotion Mechanical Painting, and the brothers Mécantre and Babisse, who are busy building a giant cannon, the projectile of which could reach the very stars of Teyvat, potentially with passengers inside it.

During the existence of the Institute of Natural Philosophy, the predecessor of the Fontaine Research Institute, Mr. Eliphas, who later became the sponsor of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo, worked at the Institute. One of his inventions, which was the result of early forays into optical science by the Institute of Natural Philosophy while they were still a budding academic organization, is the Eliphas Beam. Its basic components include "beam generators" and "beam receivers." The beam generator must sometimes be installed on a "beam receiver" base similar to a regulating valve. It can be controlled and rotated through the use of energy from a Xenochromatic Ball Octopus.

![Image 2292: Steampunk-themed airship parked in a green landscape](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2025/01/19/237301566/7589ff656dcb2a466cc9e06c0270bcaa_4269210634180498991.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

In addition to the Meks, the miraculous Antoine Roger Aircraft runs on Pneumousia energy. It's an experimental Aircraft that is propelled by energy generated from pneuma-ousia annihilation reactions. It will proceed along its set route upon being activated. Among Fontaine's many other inventions are the famous Fonta Drink, a flying energy thief, energy transfer terminals, stabilizers, water volume detection crystals, and much more. One of the devices that ran on Indemnitium and produced it was the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale, but after the death of Focalors, this type of energy is no longer available.

Fontaine is also the birthplace of rock and roll. This music is different from the traditional music of other nations, so many are skeptical about it. The Fontaines even organized a musical tour called the "Iridescence Tour," in which a rock singer from Liyue, Xinyan, wanted to perform, but circumstances prevented her. At one of the Lantern Rite Festivals, the main festival of Liyue, the tour organizer Dvorak, with the support of the Qixing, was able to hold a musical event in which Xinyan performed.
_"Rock 'n' roll is a revolution! Transforming your identity and destiny, saying goodbye to concessions and cowardice... it does them all. And most importantly, it lets you do it with art rather than words!_

_My rock 'n' roll has an unbreakable spirit, like a flame in a rainstorm that refuses to go out, or the magma that never stops boiling under the surface of the land."_

**Maison Ordalie**
==================
Fontaine is a nation of justice, so the judicial system plays a central role. Fontaine is headed by the Chief Justice Neuvillette, to whom all the other Maisons report. The judicial system is run by the Maison Ordalie, who attend court cases and pass charges. When Furina was Archon, she often attended court sessions. People could tell the importance of a case by her: if Furina was in court, the case might not be very important, but there was something absurd about it. If the Chief Justice was hearing the case, it would likely be worth attention, but often such cases cannot even be reported to journalists. During Furina's reign, sessions often resembled more of a theatrical performance, but they were still completely subject to the law.

![Image 2352: A character from Genshin Impact named Tartaglia in his Foul Legacy form](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/12/20/237301566/c7ec98269330724afc869375e13cd61c_3704465045727397892.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

All trials take place in the Opera Epiclese, formerly home to the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale, a machine created by the Hydro Archon Focalors. During the trial, the Oratrice and Neuvillette heard the testimony of both sides. The statements of the parties, the speeches of the representatives, the testimonies, and the emotions of the audience were transmitted by the Oratrice, who thus generated the Indemnitium. The Oratrice was like an independent judge, endowed with its own will, whose participation excluded any bias on the part of the Chief Justice. Thanks to this machine and the Chief Justice, false accusations and unfair sentences were almost a thing of the past. At the end of the session, the Chief Justice made the final decision, which the Oratrice took into account. Finally, the officials from the Maison requested the Oratrice's verdict, and its decision was the will of Justice itself. Except for the case when the Oratrice falsely accused the Fatui Harbinger Childe in a serial crime case, there has never been a case where the Chief Justice and the Oratrice disagreed on a verdict. Following the aftermath of Fontaine's prophecy, Neuvillette now rules alone.

![Image 2353: Two Genshin Impact characters with the left one being Neuvillette, sitting on a red and gold seat and the right one being Clorinde, holding a sword, with a torn paper effect dividing them](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/12/20/237301566/11336d37df86e17639e27a7fc9e08a69_6530323178503359102.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

In Fontaine, before a criminal goes to court, they're given one chance to defend their honor by requesting a duel with an official Champion Duelist. The Champion Duelists are all powerful fighters selected from among the nation's best, and the duel itself is a no-holds-barred fight with no specified stopping point. This profession exists to preserve dignity, but it is always accompanied by a struggle. A duel is an open-ended fight that lasts until victory, so participating in such a duel is considered a symbol of the defense of honor. If the criminal manages to win the duel, they will be acquitted, but if they lose, they'll have no choice but to stand trial. Since the challenger can die during the duel, it is usually decided by those who cannot come to terms with an unfair accusation or those who value their honor very much. The only way to end a duel is to surrender or die, and only a few manage to defeat an official Champion Duelist. One of the most famous duelists is the heir of the Marechaussee Hunters — Clorinde. Under her blade, all base actions disguised as the search for justice, and all attempts to gain profit through prosecution reveal their true nature. Clorinde has never known defeat in a duel. One of her most famous duels was the duel with Callas Caspar, president of Spina di Rosula, accused of murdering his friend and informant, Jacques. Before the duel, Callas asked Clorinde to take care of his daughter and Clorinda's friend, Navia, since he was going to die in the duel. Although he was not involved in the murder, he was ready to protect his daughter even at the cost of his life.

**Maison Gardiennage**
======================
![Image 2373: A video game character posing in front of a decorated blue door](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/12/20/237301566/ee15690c48afbc405ad108ec26615e88_9009345316813426973.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

The maintenance of public order in Fontaine is the responsibility of the Maison Gardiennage, based in the Palais Mermonia. The day-to-day defense of the city is the responsibility of the Gardemeks, special Meks created by the Fontaine Research Institute, and they are accompanied by Gardes to assist in patrols. Although the Gardemeks have advanced systems for recognizing criminals, technology is not omnipotent, and there are still many things that only humans can do. The duties of the Maison Gardiennage include protecting the Court of Fontaine and the harbors, solving crimes, finding criminals, and escorting them to Fontaine prison.

![Image 2374: A girl with long purple hair and wearing red military uniform stands on a wooden platform, in the background is a marketplace located in what appears to be a pipe tunnel](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/12/20/237301566/64fc435bece02aabd2f1e780587015ac_265687016241244459.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

If something happens that the Gardes cannot handle, the Special Surveillance and Security Patrol, which reports directly to the Chief Justice, steps in. The Special Patrol is an elite organization within the Maison Gardiennage, and they step in when, for example, prisoners resist or murderers have kidnapped a hostage. All law enforcement officers undergo rigorous background checks and training. Their every word and action represents the Maison Gardiennage and the laws of the Court of Fontaine, so there is no room for error or negligence. However, the way the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol of the Court of Fontaine does things is markedly different from other law enforcement agencies. Members are not required to use standardized weapons, nor must they wear uniforms outside of formal occasions. Additionally, after Chevreuse took command of the Special Patrol, many of its members began using muskets as part of their law enforcement arsenals, and some even began to refuse to go on missions with Gardemeks on the basis that not only can an immobile meka block their line of fire, but there's a distinct danger of criminals taking control of said meka and turning them against the squad. Furthermore, when selecting recruits, the Special Patrol will even accept the descendants of criminals whose households had been stripped of all honor. For the sake of quickly solving the most heinous of cases, the Maison Gardiennage is willing to overlook all those issues, displaying great forbearance towards Chevreuse and the Special Patrol. However, what they simply cannot abide by is how Chevreuse is willing to invite serious felons to participate in cases she is handling as "special consultants." Though Chevreuse stridently maintains that this is purely to catch vicious criminals as soon as possible, many colleagues still believe that relying on lawbreakers to help arrest lawbreakers is an insult to both the laws of Fontaine and those who enforce them.
There is a horror story for naughty children in Fontaine: _"If you don't behave, the Special Patrol's going to take you away!"_ Although children understand very clearly that the Special Patrol will never take action because a child didn't brush their teeth, it is difficult for them to suppress an involuntary shudder at the sight of the Special Patrol officers. The officers themselves are irritated by this bad reputation since it can damage their image. The Special Patrol is the official law enforcement unit of the Maison Gardiennage, and if their methods of law enforcement are harsher and the process itself more intense, it is only because the criminals they deal with are the most dangerous of all. Once, the officers even offered their captain, Chevreuse, an interview with The Steambird, but she declined the offer. _"If such a reputation has really become so deeply embedded in the minds of the people, and it sticks with them for a lifetime, then there's a chance that when someone considers taking things a step too far, fear inspired by our 'infamous reputation' may pull them back from the edge. If so, then there'll be no need for us to actually take them away someday."_

![Image 2375: Three characters from Genshin Impact stand in front of stained glass and candles; the middle character holds a sword while the character on the right holds a bow](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/06/07/237301566/b083eea6dc2eb3aa30a08919b7df4fd5_5069936352409982939.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

Another special elite organization that is part of the Maison Gardiennage and directly subordinate to the Chief Justice is the Marechaussee Phantom. The Marechaussee Phantom originated from the Marechaussee Hunters — the surviving Remurians who, under the leadership of the Harmost Cassiodor, fought the remnants of the sunken empire. The Marechaussee Phantom used to be entirely human, but now the majority are Melusines. When the Chief Justice discovered that the Melusines' unique "sight" helped in investigations, they began to be recruited to help, even though they were not strong in combat. The most significant cases in the history of the Marechaussee Phantom are the Siege of Poisson and the Battle in Elynas, during which many people died.

![Image 2376: Pearl motif with seashell and swirl design](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/02/15/237301566/c7324129b0223e4112132db8b48999f7_6667263520141079544.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

The emblem of the Maison Gardiennage depicts two Melusines. When the Chief Justice Neuvillette first brought the Melusines to the Court of Fontaine, Carole became the first Melusine in the Marechaussee Phantom. Thanks to their five years of hard work, Carole was awarded the first Medal of Peace created personally by Neuvillette. This medal further angered the supporters of the old regime, who were against the Melusines in the Court of Fontaine and whose interests were infringed upon as a result of Neuvillette's reform. They decided to commit murder and blame it on the Melusines to drive them out of the city and teach Neuvillette a lesson. They tricked Carole into coming to the crime scene and brought charges against her. After this, they sowed panic among the people in order to force Neuvillette to admit his mistakes and give up power. Carole decided to sacrifice herself to soften the situation, and the Gardes were unable to intervene in time due to the angry crowd. Carole's bravery and sacrifice ultimately led to her dream being realized: four hundred years later, the Melusines are respected members of society in the Court of Fontaine, coexisting peacefully with humans. Because of Carole's heroic deed, the emblem of the Maison Gardiennage featured Melusines as a sign of respect and gratitude to these creatures.
