**Apocalypse**
--------------
When the Traveler and Paimon arrived in Poisson in search of Furina, they heard her crying alone and talking to herself:

_"Should I just give up? This is all... meaningless..._

_What was meant to happen did happen after all. Everyone's dead..._

_I'm sorry... I'm so sorry..._

_Give up, Furina. There's no point in holding out…"_

As they approached her, she pretended that the incident at the opera house that morning had merely spoiled her enjoyment of the performance, and she disappeared to teach people a lesson. Suddenly, Furina was noticed by other people who came for her, and Paimon suggested hiding in a secret room. While they were inside, a new earthquake began, which could herald a new catastrophe. Furina admitted that she has been tirelessly exploring the mystery of the prophecy for many centuries. She once had her people all over Teyvat who collected information for her. They tried many different ways to keep the sea level so that the water did not rise, but all efforts were useless. In the end, she realized that she could not fight the Heavenly Principles, and what was predicted in the prophecy would certainly come true. Giving up in this struggle did not mean defeat for her, but coming to terms with fate, and finally being free. When people began to die, she was ready to give up, but the incident in Poisson showed that she could not decide for the Fontainians whether to surrender or continue to resist fate.

During the conversation, the "secret room" ended up on the stage of the Opera Epiclese, since everything that happened was part of the plan. The people who caused chaos in the Opera this morning were Spina di Rosula's subordinates. They changed into plain clothes, and came to the opera house as regular audience members, waiting for the perfect opportunity to incite an insurrection against the Hydro Archon. The people's resentment against their Archon has been building, so only a spark was all they needed to turn smoldering anger into a flame. They knew that Furina would most likely flee the scene and head to Poisson. The second group that pursued Furina were also members of the Spina di Rosula, and their goal was to lead Furina into the Giant Magic Box that the Fatui transported from Poisson to the Erinnyes through a dug tunnel. Clorinde and Neuvillette's task was to gather a crowd, prepare a stage, and make sure that the Champion Duelist would be immediately ready for a fight. The Traveler should have given Furina one last chance to tell the truth, but she did not take it. The interview that the Traveler and Paimon had previously given to Charlotte laid out a clear sequence of all the events that had occurred since their arrival in Fontaine, which should have helped in the prosecution process. Thus, began the great trial of the Hydro Archon.

Lady Furina was accused of posing as an Archon and deceiving the people of Fontaine as a mere mortal. The prosecution demanded that Furina touch the water of the Primordial Sea. Since no one wanted to see another dissolution, in case of unforeseen circumstances, they took a weak solution of water and called Sigewinne, the Head Nurse from the Fortress of Meropide, to conduct an examination. Not knowing that there was only a solution in the bowl, Furina dared to touch the water, but Sigewinne's examination showed that the Archon had received the same skin changes as an ordinary mortal. As a result, the Chief Justice found Furina guilty, and the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale made the final verdict: _"The Hydro Archon, guilty to be punished via the death sentence."_

![Image 2796: Drawing on the wall showing a girl with a hooded cloak hovering over a man inside a bubble, with waves and crowds of people behind her and winged creatures at the bottom](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/12/28/237301566/b0fb20592e699cd5342b9c87d6fab121_3570589706562458181.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

When the verdict was delivered, Freminet appeared in the courtroom and found the fourth stone slab with the prophecy written on it. It showed the first Hydro Archon, Egeria, releasing her divine power turning the Oceanids into human beings. In the Fontaine of old, the previous Hydro Archon sensed the yearning of her Oceanid familiars for life on land. The Oceanids were enamored with the beauty and romanticism of human beings, and, wishing to have those experiences for themselves, expressed to the Hydro Archon their desire to become of a similar kind. However, even though water as an element is intricately linked with the power of life, the Hydro Archon, as one of The Seven, did not possess the authority to create a new form of human life. Not one to give in, she eventually found a way to create permanent human bodies for her familiars by appropriating the power of this planet's Primordial Sea. She poured Primordial Sea water into the Oceanids' blood vessels, creating humanoid mimics in the process. But if Fontainians were ever to come into direct contact with water from the Primordial Sea, the power within their bodies would escape these artificial restraints and return to the Sea. As a result, their forms would collapse, and they would be reverted to their original state as Oceanids. The Hydro Archon never received permission from the Heavenly Principles to create a new "human" race, and thus, she and all of her creations came to shoulder the original sin of "appropriating the power of the Primordial Sea." The Traveler and Paimon were mistaken in thinking that the third slab should be the last: the Fontainians carried out the trial of the Hydro Archon in it, which was happening at that moment. Each step in an attempt to avoid fulfilling the prophecy only helped to make it true.

![Image 2797: Enigmatic digital illustration featuring a crystalline jellyfish hovering over a tiered platform, bathed in hues of violet, indigo, and bright teal](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/12/28/237301566/15c68a65ed9aa49b3fe80085734d56d6_5707391307571992135.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

However, if everyone saw the main threat in the flood of the Primordial Sea, it turned out to be the All-Devouring Narwhal, which the Traveler saw through Tartaglia's Vision. During the trial, a rift suddenly opened in the courtroom, through which the narwhal and the Harbinger fighting with it entered. The monster did not belong to Teyvat and had traversed the stars, weeping all the while. It had been greedily consuming the energy from the planet's Primordial Sea, using it to grow. It was his actions that led to the rise of the sea level. Since the Fontainians had the Primordial Sea in their blood, they attracted the narwhal to themselves, and, leaving the waters of the Primordial Sea, it decided to head straight to the opera house, where so many Fontainians had gathered. The narwhal absorbed too much of the Primordial Sea's energy, and at that point, had become practically integrated with the Sea itself. Even if the entirety of Teyvat were to be destroyed, it could still survive, and swim off towards some other world. Tartaglia, who fought the monster for a long time, was able to gain time, and without him, the narwhal would have reached land much earlier. Thanks to the intervention of Neuvillette and Tartaglia, the Harbinger and the narwhal disappeared back into the rift, and those gathered in court began to come up with a new plan. The words of the witch N gave hope that even if the prophecy was fulfilled, they would have a chance of salvation.

**The Opera of Noirceur and Blancheur**
---------------------------------------
![Image 2821: Furina standing in front of a mirror, which shows her original appearance](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/12/28/237301566/6b63ba3a7d5c46b0a07282251614a445_2524516851391134543.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

After the incident, Neuvillette found himself in the consciousness of the Hydro Archon, and the Traveler saw Furina's past. The real Hydro Archon was Focalors, who was once Egeria's Oceanid familiar and was turned into a human. 500 years ago, the first Hydro Archon died in the Khaenri'ahn Cataclysm and chose Focalors as her successor to the Divine Throne. Egeria knew that the prophecy would come true and that the Heavenly Principles could not be resisted. She placed the solution to this problem on the shoulders of Focalors. Focalors pondered for a long time how to counter the prophecy and found the only possible answer: it was necessary to deceive the Heavenly Principles during the fulfillment of the prophecy. After becoming an Archon, Focalors separated her newfound divinity from her body and spirit. The human counterpart she left behind, she named "Furina." After she made Furina, she also cursed her, so as long as Focalors's divinity continued to exist, Furina could not die to fulfill the prophecy. Furina was tasked to forever play the part of the god from the prophecy to create a deceitful appearance of that prophecy coming to pass. Focalors promised that Furina's torture would eventually end in a magnificent and dramatic trial, and everyone would be saved. Furina didn't know when the final trial would be, so for all these five hundred years she played her role, trying to solve the prophecy and save the people. She had to have a lot of pain and suffering, but for the sake of saving all the Fontainians, she was ready to endure it.
When Furina first took accession, she initially wanted to seem like a generous and caring god, but people considered her behavior as a weakness. Then Furina decided to become what people imagined: strong, significant, brave, and confident.

_"May law be the prayer on our lips._

_May judgment be our worship. Let us light the fires, and drink to the future of Fontaine!_

_There is no trouble in this world that justice cannot solve._

_All that is needed is for you, my people, to believe in it, heart and soul."_

For many years, Furina played her role: she participated in court sessions, received residents, and all this time she did not stop waiting for the trial that would solve everything and trying to fight the prophecy. Researchers conducted hydrological studies and tried to find a way to stop the sea level, but no one could find a solution.

182,375 "scenes"500 years

later, Furina had almost no strength left to perform this play, but she could not give up for the sake of the people of Fontaine and Focalors. When the Traveler asked her to tell the truth in the Magic Box, Furina wanted to speak out and think about herself at least once, but she never did.

![Image 2822: A bright blue anchor floats in the sky, inside an enclosed space](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/12/28/237301566/fe8ba9a40189f58b336318caf2724502_5231398309600782488.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

While Furina ruled Fontaine, Focalors accumulated energy to deceive the Heavenly Principles. She created and placed her divinity along with the Hydro Gnosis in the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale. The Oratrice converted the people's faith in justice into Indemnitium, a type of energy that powered Fontaine. Although it was used for trials, its main purpose was to kill the God of Justice along with the Divine Throne when the time came. Focalors understood that only power of this magnitude could hope to destroy the Hydro Archon's Throne. The destruction of it meant the return of the stolen power to the Hydro Dragon Sovereign, Neuvillette, whom Focalors entrusted to judge the Fontainians. As Focalors bid farewell to the Chief Justice, the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale carried out the sentence, destroying the throne of the Hydro Archon, killing Focalors, and returning full authority to the Dragon Sovereign.

![Image 2823: Anime girl with white hair and red eyes holding a purple orb](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/12/28/237301566/48f8d3d0c77024fa11df66f6e29cfe40_4981431024177322093.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

With full authority over Hydro, Neuvillette gained enough power to defeat the All-Devouring Narwhal and separate it from the Primordial Sea. Together with the Traveler, they entered the Primordial Sea, where they fought with the All-Devouring Narwhal and met Tartaglia's master, Skirk. She revealed that the monster was the pet of her master,

Surtalogi,The Foul

one of the five Sinners of Khaenri'ah. During the fight with the narwhal, energy from the Primordial Sea came to the surface and the prophecy unfolded in full force.

![Image 2824: A gigantic flying machine with architecture including domes, a clock, gears, and jets flies low to the water, with a fog-like shroud covering its lower half and the water around it](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/12/28/237301566/30e52c0f12e3a9272267dce7b8a66666_3734531003202747129.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

As predicted, all of Fontaine drowned in the water, leaving only Furina weeping on her throne. Thanks to the efforts of Fatui, Spina di Rosula, and the flying ship "Wingalet," built by the Duke of the Fortress of Meropide, the Fontainians were saved. Finally, the water receded without dissolving anyone.

**Finale**
----------
After experiencing the flood, the Fontainians began to restore the destruction. "The Steambird" journalist, Charlotte, interviewed Navia about how Champion Duelist Clorinde and the "friendly neighbors," Fatui, helped Spina di Rosula restore Poisson. At the Fortress of Meropide, researchers Lourvine and Jourie, who created the "Wingalet," also became part of Charlotte's report, as did the children of the House of the Hearth: Lyney, Lynette, and Freminet, who were again distributing the Magic Pockets. They said that the Fatui Harbinger Arlecchino received the Gnosis from Neuvillette, and Tartaglia returned to Snezhnaya to recover from his wounds.

![Image 2840: A person with long white and blue hair standing in front of a city](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/12/28/237301566/2e4606d4887212e132b884a7025ddfae_4723262396360575419.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

When Traveler and Paimon finished the interview, they returned to Neuvillette, who recounted what had happened in the courtroom. Since he gained complete control over the Hydro element, he used the ancient dragons' authority to grant the Fontainians true "blood," after the fashion in which life was first brought into being on this planet. After this, the Fontainians became ordinary people who couldn't be dissolved by the water of the Primordial Sea. In addition, he forgave them of their original sin.

When the Traveler and Paimon went to the surface during the fulfillment of the prophecy, Neuvillette stayed with Skirk, and she revealed that the Gnosis the Chief Justice had with him was the remains of the third Descender and only brought misfortune with it. That is why Neuvillette so easily parted with the Gnosis, which was useless to him, and gave it to Arlecchino.
After Focalors's death and the destruction of the Oratrice, Neuvillette became the ruler of all of Fontaine and was left alone to make decisions during the trial. Furina found her mortality and finally became free.

It shows the Traveler with Furina, Neuvillette, Navia, Freminet, Lynette, and Lyney. ](https://static0.polygonimages.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/24829982/Key_art_EN__1_.png?&fit=crop&w=1600&h=900)Image: Hoyoverse

[Genshin Impact](https://www.polygon.com/game/genshin-impact/40711/ "Genshin Impact")

[Sign in to your Polygon account](https://www.polygon.com/23820064/genshin-impact-special-program-fontaine/)

[For better or worse](https://www.polygon.com/23380882/genshin-impact-sumeru-update-inazuma-stereotype), the world of [Genshin Impact](https://www.polygon.com/reviews/23389752/genshin-impact-2022-review-hoyoverse-mihoyo-anniversary-sumeru) seems to have no bounds, and its 4.0 patch is set to introduce another new major region. Developer Hoyoverse released a new trailer for its 4.0 patch on [Friday morning as part of its livestream](https://www.polygon.com/genshin-impact-guides/23818723/patch-4-0-livestream-primogem-codes-redeem). The addition, called “As Light Rain Falls Without Reason,” will mark the introduction of the water-themed nation of Fontaine, and be released on Aug. 16.

The trailer starts with a bleak prophecy told by the magician Lyney: “The people will all be dissolved into the waters. And only the Hydro Archon will remain, weeping on her throne.” Fontaine is ruled by Focalors, the Hydro Archon and the God of Justice. Fitting to this theme, the trailer teases a trial and a mysterious device called an Oratrice, which appears to be a machine with a consciousness that can deliver sentences.

As usual, the trailer is stuffed to the brim with new characters that players can look forward to in the upcoming series of patches. We get glimpses of characters like Furina, Neuvillette, and Navia. Also, an old friend from Liyue, Childe (Tartaglia), makes his big return to the main story.

[✕ Remove Ads](https://www.polygon.com/premium/?ref=ad_removal)

As for gameplay, the 4.0 patch will introduce three new playable characters: five-star Pyro archer named Lyney; Lynette, a four-star Anemo sword-wielder; and Freminet, a four-star Cryo claymore user. On the exploration side, this region’s big addition will also allow players will be able to explore sprawling underwater regions by diving.

Lore

**Marechaussee Hunters**
========================
The name "Marechaussee Hunter" originated from Remuria, when the famous Harmost Cassiodor, who was elevated to the revered title of "Golden Hunter," guided his followers to the fight with remnants of the fallen empire: _"Pursue the phantoms in the dark, expel them all, and hunt them down."_ Though they were named "hunters," they did not hunt animals, but rather various monsters left behind by the ancient dynasty of King Remus. Today, Fontaine's monster population has already thinned greatly, so the Hunters have blended back into society, taking up arms in other lines of work. The Marechaussee Hunters of ages past would often imbue their weapons with special enchantments to suppress the monsters. Whenever a monster was nearby, their weapons would start to glow. Gradually, Marechaussee Hunters' fame faded. Today, when the people of Fontaine speak of the Marechaussee Hunters, most know only of the "Hunter's Oath," having heard it mentioned in some play or novel.

_"From this day, I pass the candle's shadow-veil."_

_"Now, as we face the perils of the long night..."_

_"I pledge to remember the oath of daylight."_

_"To enshrine tears, life, and love."_

_"Holding dawn's coming as my votive."_

_"And so shall I never despair."_

Historians believed that the Marechaussee Hunters first became active a few decades after the fall of Remuria, by which point the concept of Lochknights had completely died out in Fontaine. The first Marechaussee Hunters who followed Cassiodor were believed to be the heirs of the Lochknights, but in reality, they were the last remnants of ancient Remuria, Walter and Este. A descendant of Este inherited the responsibilities of the Golden Hunter and passed judgment on many people, and the descendant of Walter, working as an executioner, used a countless number of tricks to confound his enemies in battle. In the early days of Fontaine, the new lords who exchanged purple robes for noble titles swore an oath before the sword of lakelight with disparate motives, and then interpreted the laws and justice as they pleased. These genealogies of High Sea kingship and heroism did not lack gracious benefactors, but neither were they bereft of ambitious schemers or wicked broods of selfish greed that festered in the shadows, those who wore masks of loyalty to gild their wild obsession with wealth and power, who supped of the resentment and suffering of the poor like it was crimson wine in a goblet. Walter's descendant, despite the Golden Hunter's orders to stay away from the squabbles of that great city, lest their blades be stained with the blood of their brethren, decided to go to war again against the descendants of the rulers of the northern kingdoms to defend justice. Forsaking the longsword that was the Golden Hunter's heritage, he wielded now a shortbow, and like a shadow, he stalked between the high halls, using blood to paint the gallows-noose of judgment. And although the tractor was executed and later exonerated, the techniques that had silently ended so many noble lives, the archery meant to pierce the throats of the oppressors, and the steps meant to evade pursuit were not lost. In sponsored operas, the rebel was celebrated as the Executioner of the Marechausse Hunters, an idol defanged and harmless. And per the will of those in power, the Marechaussee Hunters began to pass on the secret techniques from generation to generation.

There is a tale of a Marechaussee Hunter who became obsessed with exterminating monsters. When the day came that the land had been cleansed of their shadow, it didn't take long before he began to feel lost. After a life spent hunting monsters, what purpose did his life have now that their mortal enemy had been vanquished? After giving the matter much thought, he decided to carry on living as he had, severing his connections with the Marechaussee Hunters so that he might continue hunting down monsters alone. This tale is a reminder that the Marechaussee Hunters fight to restore peace to everyone's lives. It's important to remember what you're fighting for, and never let the means become the end.

![Image 72: Character in a dark blue and black steampunk-style uniform is striking a pose with her arms slightly raised, one hand holding a gun and the other holding a thin, pointed weapon, and she is surrounded by purple energy effects](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/06/07/237301566/a850a2c6fcd9b1468760e556f2e6d706_1656471766893106077.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

For most Fontainians, the story of the Marechaussee Hunters is now but a legend full of drama and excitement. To the Champion Duelist Clorinde, the deeds and oaths of the Hunters are her living, breathing inheritance. The first thing she learned from her mentor, the Marechaussee Hunter Petronilla, was the swordsmanship required to slay monsters. The approach of the Hunter requires them to stay as close as possible to their prey so that they might plunge their blade into weak points with lightning-fast agility. To train her in this technique, Petronilla consigned Clorinde to a room filled with rotating pillars, each of which had been set up with many wooden swords protruding outwards, their tips covered with cloth bags. By undergoing such training, Clorinde not only developed the Marechaussee Hunter's skills of marksmanship, tracking, camouflage, and footwork. Her choice of weapons follows the Marechaussee Hunter tradition: a Musket to chase away the prey, and a sword to deliver a fatal strike.

![Image 73: Interior of a church with a strange, purple cloud in front of the altar and two sconces on the wall](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/06/07/237301566/080b908b0847e4ab8e6623f146a4c630_6705713600194936073.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

One day, one of the successors of the Marechaussee Hunters, Florian, succumbed to the influence of the monster, the Devorator, which raged several centuries ago. Florian's father was a Hunter and devoted his entire life to serving the cause, but in return, he received only poverty and suffering. When he died, no one even came to say goodbye to him. Members of his family had been Marechaussee Hunters for generations, passing down not only the title and swordsmanship but also a seal the Marechaussee Hunters used to restrain the Devorator, hoping that in time a way would be found to defeat it. Florian's father instructed him to always watch over that seal and maintain it regularly since it was the most important duty of his clan. However, after his death, his son abandoned this duty. The Devorator was a dangerous opponent even for the Hunters, and if a mortal had enough strength to destroy it, the person became a victim of its corruption. The creature was able to amplify the obsessions and desires in people's hearts, to the point where they overtook them entirely. When Florian finally decided to check the seal, the monster took over his consciousness. The anger over injustice in Florian's soul made him easy prey.

![Image 74: An ornate stone pillar sits in a cave, surrounded by swords stuck in the ground](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/06/07/237301566/a24ab9c0c1c60326303c3e3eb8f2cf0b_5984861954135643665.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

Under the guise of the plot of a role-playing game, Florian lured Clorinde, Lyney, Furina, Navia, the Traveler, and Paimon into the secret treasury of the Marechaussee Hunters in order to destroy the Hunters and take the treasures that he believed were rightfully his. To open the treasury, he lacked only one key out of four: one was given to him by his father, he stole the other, took the third from a Hunter, and the missing key was given to Clorinde by her mentor. 

![Image 75: Three anime characters in the interior of a church-like building](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/06/07/237301566/b083eea6dc2eb3aa30a08919b7df4fd5_4080773771820532161.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

During the battle, Clorinde temporarily expelled the monster from the man's body. When they opened the door of the treasury, it turned out that it hid a stone tablet with the names of the Hunters carved into it and their weapons, which they decided to take with them to defeat the Devorator: Furina had the sword of Cassiodor's friend, Este, and Lyney had Walter's bow. Navia used Petronilla's sword, which Clorinde gave her after the duel with her father. Florian lured the monster into his body to defeat the monster, and Clorinde, Navia, Furina, Lyney, the Traveler, and Paimon defeated it with the help of the Hunters' spirits.

**Marechaussee Phantom**
========================
The Marechaussee Phantom is the Chief Justice Neuvillette's personal unit, which is responsible for crime investigation. The Marechaussee Phantom is based in the Palais Mermonia and is one of the Maison Gardiennage's departments. The organization used to be comprised only of humans, but now the majority of them are Melusines, as their special visual acuity was most suited to investigating cases.

Many Marechaussee Phantom members, including Emanuel Guillotin, originated from the Narzissenkreuz Institute — a child orphanage in Fontaine, where the children of criminals were often sent. The orphanage was ruled by the Director Lyris, an Oceanid, and, for a while, the former Navy admiral, Basil Elton, was the Vice Director. When the Institute disbanded 500 years ago because of the Cataclysm, many students joined the Marechaussee Phantom or the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol to protect Fontaine such that it would not again have a shadow cast over it.

Some of the Marechaussee Phantom agents, members who undertake investigations, work secretly, and their names are confidential. Thus, no files were left about the agents who died during the battle in Elynas.

**Siege of Poisson**
====================
More than 500 years ago, the authorities of Fontaine wanted to create an undercity beneath the city, the Fleuve Cendre, from the sewers in the Court of Fontaine. Since it was difficult to maintain order, Eduardo Baker and his friends seized power in the sewers. They began to resolve disputes between the Fleuve Cendre "compatriots," bless the newly wedded, and protect the merchants from being extorted, harassed, and blackmailed by the gangs. When the authorities of the Court of Fontaine decided to purge the Fleuve Cendre, Baker was arrested and exiled to the desert. On the way to exile, he, with the help of his henchmen, fled to Poisson, taking hostage both the city itself and the members of the Maison Gardiennage who were transporting Baker. He made several unreasonable demands, so the Marechaussee Hunters, under the direction of Emanuel Guillotin, intervened. Journalist Karl Ingold arrived in Poisson as a negotiator along with Eduardo's son, Jakob.

Following an unsuccessful attempt to resolve the issue, the disagreement between Baker's group and the Marechaussee Hunters turned into a violent fight. As a result, Jakob and Rene, the Poisson Mayor's son, were left orphans. They were both sent to the Narzissenkreuz Institute. Later, these two children founded The Narzissenkreuz Ordo, one of the most important organizations in Fontaine's History.

The Siege of Poisson left physical and mental scars on Guillotin. Due to this event, he left the ranks of the Marechaussee and planned to live out the rest of his days, content with just the contents of his cup. When the Cataclysm began, his old friend from the Narzissenkreuz Institute, Basil Elton, entrusted him with two children: Mary-Ann and Alain. Emanuel had no love for children and wished to have no dealings with anyone, but for the sake of his old friend, he agreed.

**The Narzissenkreuz Ordo**
===========================
![Image 147: The Genshin Impact-style cartoon illustration features an adult female and four children in a variety of outfits, set against a background with what appears to be a large symbol](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/04/18/237301566/9dd957087aa42735905d94761558de17_7036168828870711319.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

Roughly 500 years ago, four children from the Narzissenkreuz Institute became friends. After the Cataclysm, two of them, Mary-Ann and Alain, were adopted by the former Marechaussee Hunter, Emanuel Guillotin, and later became Marechaussee Phantom agents themselves. The others, Rene and Jakob, who were sent to the Institute because of Emanuel Guillotin, were taken by the journalist, Karl Ingold, who was present in the Siege of Poisson. Years later, they founded an organization called the Narzissenkreuz Ordo.

![Image 148: A character from the game Genshin Impact is in a battle stance with a glowing light behind them](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/04/18/237301566/11e84dca9047c764fbdde904a7970dbf_7218597961318265236.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

The main purpose of the organization was to save Fontaine from the apocalypse predicted by the prophecy: _"In the end, the people will all be dissolved into the waters, and only the Hydro Archon will remain, weeping on her throne."_ To achieve that, they started conducting immoral and dangerous experiments, which included the creation of Neohumans. The leader, known as

the "Master"Rene de Petrichor

 wanted to dissolve all Fontainians by the Primordial waters to wait out the apocalypse and be reborn in the new world.

Once, Emanuel Guillotin's friend confided in him about his concerns about the operations of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo. This investigation was the last one for Guillotin. Judging by the fact that in the end, he recalled his "children" and the embrace of Director Lyris, who by that time was a member of this organization; and Master in his notes mentions the absorption of several agents of the Marechaussee Hunters with the help of the Oceanid, it can be assumed that Emanuel, as well as the Champion Duelist Marfisa, was one of these agents.
_"My dear Alain, my dear Mary-Ann... I was never close to you,"_

_"And even at the end, I do not know how I could be a "father" to you."_

_"But still, I do not wish to lose these memories of watching the two of you growing up..."_

_— When he awoke from his stupor, all glories, all shame, all love and obsession — they had been dissolved in the waters._

_"At the end, that which welcomed him was a peaceful ocean, one which removed all barriers and estrangements."_

![Image 149: Two anime characters, one with short brown hair and the other with long white hair and blue highlights, stand side by side in a sepia-toned landscape](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/04/18/237301566/4a244b78de17042e111af3c05e389473_4299516187377096920.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

When the authorities found out about these experiments and the dissolution of people, the Narzissenkreuz Ordo was declared radical. Alain Guillotin broke off all relations with his friends, Rene and Jakob, and, together with Fontaine's Iudex, Neuvillette, signed the order for the Narzissenkreuz Ordo destruction.

To buy some time to execute his plans, the Master sent Jakob, former Director of the Narzissenkreuz Institute, Lyris, and other members of the Ordo to the petrified body of Elynas. Elynas was an Abyssal beast, who appeared in Fontaine during the Cataclysm. When he died, the Narzissenkreuz Ordo used his blood and flesh in their experiments, creating the first Neohuman from Jakob. To help Jakob obtain greater abilities and distract the Marechaussee Hunters from the Master, the Narzissenkreuz Ordo decided to revive Elynas's petrified heart. When Alain Guillotin found out about the upcoming ritual, he sent a thinking Mek, Seymour, to inform the Iudex of Fontaine Neuvillette about it.
When the agents of the Marechaussee Phantom, including Mary-Ann Guillotin, tracked down the Ordo members in Elynas's body, a battle occurred. Many agents and the Meks were killed due to the explosion. Mary-Ann Guillotin was on the verge of death, but she was saved by Lyris. Lyris united their bodies and minds by hugging her, creating a new Oceanid, Mary-Ann.

After the battle in Elynas, Alain Guillotin never heard from his sister. He left the Marechaussee Phantom and founded the Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering. There is a legend that in his old age, Alain retired from the Fontaine Research Institute to his workshop, and he would see no one. The research he undertook in his final years was never published, and after the matter, the only things that could be found in his workshop were signs that something had been built.

**Melusines**
=============
![Image 183: A stylized, fantasy landscape features mushroom houses and glowing lights, all under an overarching network of trees and a purple, blue, and pink palette](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/02/17/237301566/48c2f788c6d4baea0ff56bb9f5c61e18_2534850688729486975.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

Nowadays, the Marechaussee Phantom comprises mostly of the Melusines, but roughly 400 years ago, there was not a single Melusine in the unit and the Court of Fontaine. Carole, like other Melusines, was born from wounds received by their "Father," Elynas, during the battle between the Marechaussee Hunters and members of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo more than 400 years ago. The Melusines lived in the Merusea Village, which they built inside the Elynas's body. They learned how to build houses from their "Father." Twenty years later, some Melusines wanted to go to the Court of Fontaine to see how people lived and find the meaning of their existence. Carole became one of the first Melusines who, with the help of the young Iudex of Fontaine, Neuvillette, a Hydro Dragon, entered the Court of Fontaine.

![Image 184: Black and white image features a small bunny eared person wearing a tunic and an adult character with long flowing hair](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/02/17/237301566/54d819f57d56d4e686846c2fd51f6051_4559846552267452481.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

Since all Melusines have a special vision and are able to notice things that are inaccessible to the human eye, Neuvillette invited them to the Marechaussee Phantom — a special branch of the Maison Gardiennage responsible for investigating crimes. Carole became the first Melusine in the Marechaussee Phantom, and the leader of the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol, Vautrin, was assigned as her partner. The people of the Court of Fontaine had never seen Melusines before, so they treated them with caution and dissatisfaction, as there were rumors that Melusines were creatures of disaster that posed a danger to others. They threw stones at the Melusines and told them to return to their village. Neuvillette and Carole knew that it would take a lot of time and effort for people and Melusines to live in harmony and understanding, but Carole was ready for this long and difficult path, as her life became more meaningful.

![Image 185: Sea Ganoderma is a local specialty of Inazuma that can be found on the shores of the islands](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/02/17/237301566/c7324129b0223e4112132db8b48999f7_4126101012701089002.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

Thanks to their hard work for five years, Carole and the leader of the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol, Vautrin, were awarded the first Medals of Peace from Neuvillette. Carole hoped that the Melusines would soon begin to live peacefully with people, but this medal only further angered the supporters of the old regime, whose interests were infringed upon as a result of Neuvillette's reform. They decided to commit murder and blame it on the Melusines to drive them out of the city and teach Neuvillette a lesson.

Supporters of the old regime tricked Carole to come to the crime scene and brought charges against her. After this, they sowed panic among the people in order to force Neuvillette to admit his mistakes and give up power. Carole decided to sacrifice herself to soften the situation, and the Gardes were unable to intervene in time due to the angry crowd.
Vautrin, having learned about what had happened, decided to avenge Carole and personally killed all the conspirators. He knew that Neuvillette would be forced to declare him guilty and exile him to the Fortress of Meropide, but he could not help but intervene. Carole reminded Vautrin of his younger sister, Illaria, who died when he was little. Carole and Illaria were both kind and innocent, and they always believed in the best. Vautrin understood that kind souls like Carole were more susceptible to deception and betrayal, so he tried to force her to retreat so that people would not harm her.

Carole's bravery and sacrifice ultimately led to her dream being realized: 400 years later, the Melusines are respected members of society in the Court of Fontaine, coexisting peacefully with humans. Because of Carole's heroic deed, the emblem of the Maison Gardiennage featured Melusines as a sign of respect and gratitude to these creatures.

When 400 years later, another Melusine, Kiara, was threatened by some criminals, citizens of the Court of Fontaine united to protect her. "The Steambird" reporter, Charlotte, asked her colleagues about the threat letter. Clorinde, the Champion Duelist, offered her help to protect Kiara. Spina di Rosula's president, Navia, asked her people to keep an eye out for leads and "invited" the suspects for coffee so they couldn't resist. With their help, criminals were found, and Melusines were not harmed.

**Marechaussee Hunters**
========================
The name "Marechaussee Hunter" originated from Remuria, when the famous Harmost Cassiodor, who was elevated to the revered title of "Golden Hunter," guided his followers to the fight with remnants of the fallen empire: _"Pursue the phantoms in the dark, expel them all, and hunt them down."_ Though they were named "hunters," they did not hunt animals, but rather various monsters left behind by the ancient dynasty of King Remus. Today, Fontaine's monster population has already thinned greatly, so the Hunters have blended back into society, taking up arms in other lines of work. The Marechaussee Hunters of ages past would often imbue their weapons with special enchantments to suppress the monsters. Whenever a monster was nearby, their weapons would start to glow. Gradually, Marechaussee Hunters' fame faded. Today, when the people of Fontaine speak of the Marechaussee Hunters, most know only of the "Hunter's Oath," having heard it mentioned in some play or novel.

_"From this day, I pass the candle's shadow-veil."_

_"Now, as we face the perils of the long night..."_

_"I pledge to remember the oath of daylight."_

_"To enshrine tears, life, and love."_

_"Holding dawn's coming as my votive."_

_"And so shall I never despair."_

Historians believed that the Marechaussee Hunters first became active a few decades after the fall of Remuria, by which point the concept of Lochknights had completely died out in Fontaine. The first Marechaussee Hunters who followed Cassiodor were believed to be the heirs of the Lochknights, but in reality, they were the last remnants of ancient Remuria, Walter and Este. A descendant of Este inherited the responsibilities of the Golden Hunter and passed judgment on many people, and the descendant of Walter, working as an executioner, used a countless number of tricks to confound his enemies in battle. In the early days of Fontaine, the new lords who exchanged purple robes for noble titles swore an oath before the sword of lakelight with disparate motives, and then interpreted the laws and justice as they pleased. These genealogies of High Sea kingship and heroism did not lack gracious benefactors, but neither were they bereft of ambitious schemers or wicked broods of selfish greed that festered in the shadows, those who wore masks of loyalty to gild their wild obsession with wealth and power, who supped of the resentment and suffering of the poor like it was crimson wine in a goblet. Walter's descendant, despite the Golden Hunter's orders to stay away from the squabbles of that great city, lest their blades be stained with the blood of their brethren, decided to go to war again against the descendants of the rulers of the northern kingdoms to defend justice. Forsaking the longsword that was the Golden Hunter's heritage, he wielded now a shortbow, and like a shadow, he stalked between the high halls, using blood to paint the gallows-noose of judgment. And although the tractor was executed and later exonerated, the techniques that had silently ended so many noble lives, the archery meant to pierce the throats of the oppressors, and the steps meant to evade pursuit were not lost. In sponsored operas, the rebel was celebrated as the Executioner of the Marechausse Hunters, an idol defanged and harmless. And per the will of those in power, the Marechaussee Hunters began to pass on the secret techniques from generation to generation.

There is a tale of a Marechaussee Hunter who became obsessed with exterminating monsters. When the day came that the land had been cleansed of their shadow, it didn't take long before he began to feel lost. After a life spent hunting monsters, what purpose did his life have now that their mortal enemy had been vanquished? After giving the matter much thought, he decided to carry on living as he had, severing his connections with the Marechaussee Hunters so that he might continue hunting down monsters alone. This tale is a reminder that the Marechaussee Hunters fight to restore peace to everyone's lives. It's important to remember what you're fighting for, and never let the means become the end.

![Image 245: Character in a dark blue and black steampunk-style uniform is striking a pose with her arms slightly raised, one hand holding a gun and the other holding a thin, pointed weapon, and she is surrounded by purple energy effects](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/06/07/237301566/a850a2c6fcd9b1468760e556f2e6d706_1656471766893106077.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

For most Fontainians, the story of the Marechaussee Hunters is now but a legend full of drama and excitement. To the Champion Duelist Clorinde, the deeds and oaths of the Hunters are her living, breathing inheritance. The first thing she learned from her mentor, the Marechaussee Hunter Petronilla, was the swordsmanship required to slay monsters. The approach of the Hunter requires them to stay as close as possible to their prey so that they might plunge their blade into weak points with lightning-fast agility. To train her in this technique, Petronilla consigned Clorinde to a room filled with rotating pillars, each of which had been set up with many wooden swords protruding outwards, their tips covered with cloth bags. By undergoing such training, Clorinde not only developed the Marechaussee Hunter's skills of marksmanship, tracking, camouflage, and footwork. Her choice of weapons follows the Marechaussee Hunter tradition: a Musket to chase away the prey, and a sword to deliver a fatal strike.

![Image 246: Interior of a church with a strange, purple cloud in front of the altar and two sconces on the wall](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/06/07/237301566/080b908b0847e4ab8e6623f146a4c630_6705713600194936073.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

One day, one of the successors of the Marechaussee Hunters, Florian, succumbed to the influence of the monster, the Devorator, which raged several centuries ago. Florian's father was a Hunter and devoted his entire life to serving the cause, but in return, he received only poverty and suffering. When he died, no one even came to say goodbye to him. Members of his family had been Marechaussee Hunters for generations, passing down not only the title and swordsmanship but also a seal the Marechaussee Hunters used to restrain the Devorator, hoping that in time a way would be found to defeat it. Florian's father instructed him to always watch over that seal and maintain it regularly since it was the most important duty of his clan. However, after his death, his son abandoned this duty. The Devorator was a dangerous opponent even for the Hunters, and if a mortal had enough strength to destroy it, the person became a victim of its corruption. The creature was able to amplify the obsessions and desires in people's hearts, to the point where they overtook them entirely. When Florian finally decided to check the seal, the monster took over his consciousness. The anger over injustice in Florian's soul made him easy prey.

![Image 247: An ornate stone pillar sits in a cave, surrounded by swords stuck in the ground](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/06/07/237301566/a24ab9c0c1c60326303c3e3eb8f2cf0b_5984861954135643665.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

Under the guise of the plot of a role-playing game, Florian lured Clorinde, Lyney, Furina, Navia, the Traveler, and Paimon into the secret treasury of the Marechaussee Hunters in order to destroy the Hunters and take the treasures that he believed were rightfully his. To open the treasury, he lacked only one key out of four: one was given to him by his father, he stole the other, took the third from a Hunter, and the missing key was given to Clorinde by her mentor. 

![Image 248: Three anime characters in the interior of a church-like building](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/06/07/237301566/b083eea6dc2eb3aa30a08919b7df4fd5_4080773771820532161.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

During the battle, Clorinde temporarily expelled the monster from the man's body. When they opened the door of the treasury, it turned out that it hid a stone tablet with the names of the Hunters carved into it and their weapons, which they decided to take with them to defeat the Devorator: Furina had the sword of Cassiodor's friend, Este, and Lyney had Walter's bow. Navia used Petronilla's sword, which Clorinde gave her after the duel with her father. Florian lured the monster into his body to defeat the monster, and Clorinde, Navia, Furina, Lyney, the Traveler, and Paimon defeated it with the help of the Hunters' spirits.

**Marechaussee Phantom**
========================
The Marechaussee Phantom is the Chief Justice Neuvillette's personal unit, which is responsible for crime investigation. The Marechaussee Phantom is based in the Palais Mermonia and is one of the Maison Gardiennage's departments. The organization used to be comprised only of humans, but now the majority of them are Melusines, as their special visual acuity was most suited to investigating cases.

Many Marechaussee Phantom members, including Emanuel Guillotin, originated from the Narzissenkreuz Institute — a child orphanage in Fontaine, where the children of criminals were often sent. The orphanage was ruled by the Director Lyris, an Oceanid, and, for a while, the former Navy admiral, Basil Elton, was the Vice Director. When the Institute disbanded 500 years ago because of the Cataclysm, many students joined the Marechaussee Phantom or the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol to protect Fontaine such that it would not again have a shadow cast over it.

Some of the Marechaussee Phantom agents, members who undertake investigations, work secretly, and their names are confidential. Thus, no files were left about the agents who died during the battle in Elynas.

**Siege of Poisson**
====================
More than 500 years ago, the authorities of Fontaine wanted to create an undercity beneath the city, the Fleuve Cendre, from the sewers in the Court of Fontaine. Since it was difficult to maintain order, Eduardo Baker and his friends seized power in the sewers. They began to resolve disputes between the Fleuve Cendre "compatriots," bless the newly wedded, and protect the merchants from being extorted, harassed, and blackmailed by the gangs. When the authorities of the Court of Fontaine decided to purge the Fleuve Cendre, Baker was arrested and exiled to the desert. On the way to exile, he, with the help of his henchmen, fled to Poisson, taking hostage both the city itself and the members of the Maison Gardiennage who were transporting Baker. He made several unreasonable demands, so the Marechaussee Hunters, under the direction of Emanuel Guillotin, intervened. Journalist Karl Ingold arrived in Poisson as a negotiator along with Eduardo's son, Jakob.

Following an unsuccessful attempt to resolve the issue, the disagreement between Baker's group and the Marechaussee Hunters turned into a violent fight. As a result, Jakob and Rene, the Poisson Mayor's son, were left orphans. They were both sent to the Narzissenkreuz Institute. Later, these two children founded The Narzissenkreuz Ordo, one of the most important organizations in Fontaine's History.

The Siege of Poisson left physical and mental scars on Guillotin. Due to this event, he left the ranks of the Marechaussee and planned to live out the rest of his days, content with just the contents of his cup. When the Cataclysm began, his old friend from the Narzissenkreuz Institute, Basil Elton, entrusted him with two children: Mary-Ann and Alain. Emanuel had no love for children and wished to have no dealings with anyone, but for the sake of his old friend, he agreed.

**The Narzissenkreuz Ordo**
===========================
![Image 320: The Genshin Impact-style cartoon illustration features an adult female and four children in a variety of outfits, set against a background with what appears to be a large symbol](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/04/18/237301566/9dd957087aa42735905d94761558de17_7036168828870711319.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

Roughly 500 years ago, four children from the Narzissenkreuz Institute became friends. After the Cataclysm, two of them, Mary-Ann and Alain, were adopted by the former Marechaussee Hunter, Emanuel Guillotin, and later became Marechaussee Phantom agents themselves. The others, Rene and Jakob, who were sent to the Institute because of Emanuel Guillotin, were taken by the journalist, Karl Ingold, who was present in the Siege of Poisson. Years later, they founded an organization called the Narzissenkreuz Ordo.

![Image 321: A character from the game Genshin Impact is in a battle stance with a glowing light behind them](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/04/18/237301566/11e84dca9047c764fbdde904a7970dbf_7218597961318265236.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

The main purpose of the organization was to save Fontaine from the apocalypse predicted by the prophecy: _"In the end, the people will all be dissolved into the waters, and only the Hydro Archon will remain, weeping on her throne."_ To achieve that, they started conducting immoral and dangerous experiments, which included the creation of Neohumans. The leader, known as

the "Master"Rene de Petrichor

 wanted to dissolve all Fontainians by the Primordial waters to wait out the apocalypse and be reborn in the new world.

Once, Emanuel Guillotin's friend confided in him about his concerns about the operations of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo. This investigation was the last one for Guillotin. Judging by the fact that in the end, he recalled his "children" and the embrace of Director Lyris, who by that time was a member of this organization; and Master in his notes mentions the absorption of several agents of the Marechaussee Hunters with the help of the Oceanid, it can be assumed that Emanuel, as well as the Champion Duelist Marfisa, was one of these agents.
_"My dear Alain, my dear Mary-Ann... I was never close to you,"_

_"And even at the end, I do not know how I could be a "father" to you."_

_"But still, I do not wish to lose these memories of watching the two of you growing up..."_

_— When he awoke from his stupor, all glories, all shame, all love and obsession — they had been dissolved in the waters._

_"At the end, that which welcomed him was a peaceful ocean, one which removed all barriers and estrangements."_

![Image 322: Two anime characters, one with short brown hair and the other with long white hair and blue highlights, stand side by side in a sepia-toned landscape](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/04/18/237301566/4a244b78de17042e111af3c05e389473_4299516187377096920.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

When the authorities found out about these experiments and the dissolution of people, the Narzissenkreuz Ordo was declared radical. Alain Guillotin broke off all relations with his friends, Rene and Jakob, and, together with Fontaine's Iudex, Neuvillette, signed the order for the Narzissenkreuz Ordo destruction.

To buy some time to execute his plans, the Master sent Jakob, former Director of the Narzissenkreuz Institute, Lyris, and other members of the Ordo to the petrified body of Elynas. Elynas was an Abyssal beast, who appeared in Fontaine during the Cataclysm. When he died, the Narzissenkreuz Ordo used his blood and flesh in their experiments, creating the first Neohuman from Jakob. To help Jakob obtain greater abilities and distract the Marechaussee Hunters from the Master, the Narzissenkreuz Ordo decided to revive Elynas's petrified heart. When Alain Guillotin found out about the upcoming ritual, he sent a thinking Mek, Seymour, to inform the Iudex of Fontaine Neuvillette about it.
When the agents of the Marechaussee Phantom, including Mary-Ann Guillotin, tracked down the Ordo members in Elynas's body, a battle occurred. Many agents and the Meks were killed due to the explosion. Mary-Ann Guillotin was on the verge of death, but she was saved by Lyris. Lyris united their bodies and minds by hugging her, creating a new Oceanid, Mary-Ann.

After the battle in Elynas, Alain Guillotin never heard from his sister. He left the Marechaussee Phantom and founded the Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering. There is a legend that in his old age, Alain retired from the Fontaine Research Institute to his workshop, and he would see no one. The research he undertook in his final years was never published, and after the matter, the only things that could be found in his workshop were signs that something had been built.

**Melusines**
=============
![Image 356: A stylized, fantasy landscape features mushroom houses and glowing lights, all under an overarching network of trees and a purple, blue, and pink palette](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/02/17/237301566/48c2f788c6d4baea0ff56bb9f5c61e18_2534850688729486975.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

Nowadays, the Marechaussee Phantom comprises mostly of the Melusines, but roughly 400 years ago, there was not a single Melusine in the unit and the Court of Fontaine. Carole, like other Melusines, was born from wounds received by their "Father," Elynas, during the battle between the Marechaussee Hunters and members of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo more than 400 years ago. The Melusines lived in the Merusea Village, which they built inside the Elynas's body. They learned how to build houses from their "Father." Twenty years later, some Melusines wanted to go to the Court of Fontaine to see how people lived and find the meaning of their existence. Carole became one of the first Melusines who, with the help of the young Iudex of Fontaine, Neuvillette, a Hydro Dragon, entered the Court of Fontaine.

![Image 357: Black and white image features a small bunny eared person wearing a tunic and an adult character with long flowing hair](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/02/17/237301566/54d819f57d56d4e686846c2fd51f6051_4559846552267452481.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

Since all Melusines have a special vision and are able to notice things that are inaccessible to the human eye, Neuvillette invited them to the Marechaussee Phantom — a special branch of the Maison Gardiennage responsible for investigating crimes. Carole became the first Melusine in the Marechaussee Phantom, and the leader of the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol, Vautrin, was assigned as her partner. The people of the Court of Fontaine had never seen Melusines before, so they treated them with caution and dissatisfaction, as there were rumors that Melusines were creatures of disaster that posed a danger to others. They threw stones at the Melusines and told them to return to their village. Neuvillette and Carole knew that it would take a lot of time and effort for people and Melusines to live in harmony and understanding, but Carole was ready for this long and difficult path, as her life became more meaningful.

![Image 358: Sea Ganoderma is a local specialty of Inazuma that can be found on the shores of the islands](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/02/17/237301566/c7324129b0223e4112132db8b48999f7_4126101012701089002.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

Thanks to their hard work for five years, Carole and the leader of the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol, Vautrin, were awarded the first Medals of Peace from Neuvillette. Carole hoped that the Melusines would soon begin to live peacefully with people, but this medal only further angered the supporters of the old regime, whose interests were infringed upon as a result of Neuvillette's reform. They decided to commit murder and blame it on the Melusines to drive them out of the city and teach Neuvillette a lesson.

Supporters of the old regime tricked Carole to come to the crime scene and brought charges against her. After this, they sowed panic among the people in order to force Neuvillette to admit his mistakes and give up power. Carole decided to sacrifice herself to soften the situation, and the Gardes were unable to intervene in time due to the angry crowd.
Vautrin, having learned about what had happened, decided to avenge Carole and personally killed all the conspirators. He knew that Neuvillette would be forced to declare him guilty and exile him to the Fortress of Meropide, but he could not help but intervene. Carole reminded Vautrin of his younger sister, Illaria, who died when he was little. Carole and Illaria were both kind and innocent, and they always believed in the best. Vautrin understood that kind souls like Carole were more susceptible to deception and betrayal, so he tried to force her to retreat so that people would not harm her.

Carole's bravery and sacrifice ultimately led to her dream being realized: 400 years later, the Melusines are respected members of society in the Court of Fontaine, coexisting peacefully with humans. Because of Carole's heroic deed, the emblem of the Maison Gardiennage featured Melusines as a sign of respect and gratitude to these creatures.

When 400 years later, another Melusine, Kiara, was threatened by some criminals, citizens of the Court of Fontaine united to protect her. "The Steambird" reporter, Charlotte, asked her colleagues about the threat letter. Clorinde, the Champion Duelist, offered her help to protect Kiara. Spina di Rosula's president, Navia, asked her people to keep an eye out for leads and "invited" the suspects for coffee so they couldn't resist. With their help, criminals were found, and Melusines were not harmed.

**Court of Fontaine**
---------------------
![Image 201: Exterior of a building that appears to be from the game Genshin Impact with banners flanking the door, and a young girl wearing a dark-blue dress](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/08/10/237301566/fa022188ba97fd603de68ffb1b0e2021_6886117796016874432.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

The Court of Fontaine is the main city of Fontaine, where the residence of the last Hydro Archon Furina was located. The Court of Fontaine can be reached via the Clementine aquabus line, leading from Romaritime Harbor. The city amazes with its sophistication, majesty, and technology. One of the main attractions of the city is the Statue of the Seven, located near the Palais Mermonia. Gardemeks can be seen on the streets keeping order, as well as Melusines from the Marechaussee Phantom, and smartly dressed ladies and their dogs.

![Image 202: Large display in the center of a building with a poster and golden decor](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/08/10/237301566/2d636b97f8448c8c627cac878cdad86d_3285924680632916599.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

The Fontinalia Festival takes place in the Court of Fontaine. It was established to honor the legendary Lochknights who searched for the Oceanids and welcomed the first Hydro Archon Egeria. Similar to other prominent festivals like Mondstadt's Windblume Festival and Liyue's Lantern Rite, it holds deep connections to the founding of Fontaine, making it one of the nation's most important festivals. Originally, people commemorated the Lochknights by imitating them, wearing special costumes, raising golden cups, and going door-to-door requesting pure water. However, Furina made the tradition more festive a few years ago by changing the water request to sweets. The festival is considered to be more carnival-like now and is popular among children who engage in "trial or treat" activities each year which include going door-to-door asking for candies with baskets during the celebration. During the first Fontinalia Festival, the Traveler and Paimon attended, and the prestigious "Furina Award," named after the former Hydro Archon Lady Furina, was given out at the end of the festival. Despite the changes in leadership, the name is still fitting for the award as Furina remains a beloved figure in Fontaine.

One day, Lepine-Pauline, a specialist in Graph Adversarial Technology, decided to use an improved Kamera lens to rid Teyvat of everyone out there who's trying to con innocent people. She read in The Steambird that _"Several keen-eyed thieves who noticed a flaw in the Gardemeks detection systems disguised themselves as Blubberbeasts during the commission of their crimes."_ Completely blind to the would-be-Blubberbeasts, the Gardemeks made no attempt to intervene in the thefts committed by the gang. She had an idea that it was possible to improve the Gardemeks' ability to recognize targets in order to recognize criminals in disguise. Lepine-Pauline decided to collect sample images and, based on them, develop a simple but powerful and highly accurate image recognition algorithm that runs on a small graphical processing module. Any clockwork meka installed with this module would instantly be able to recognize people wearing disguises and accurately assess the criminal threat they pose. She hoped that her invention would make her incredibly rich and even borrowed a large sum from the bank to develop her technology.

It turned out that the news in The Steambird was a short story mailed to them by an anonymous amateur author, written in the style of a true story. Although the editors of the newspaper were afraid that the story could mislead readers, the Maison Gardiennage supported them in printing it. They figured that the false intel would be a great way to dupe potential criminals into wearing ridiculous costumes when breaking the law. Since the publication of this story, the Maison Gardiennage has made a slew of arrests including "Phantom Blubberbeast," a "Titanic Redcrown Finch," and a "Specterman" as the recognition function of the Gardemeks worked perfectly. Lepine-Pauline was ready to fight the Gardemeks to be sent to the Fortress of Meropide in order not to pay off the loan, but the newspaper's journalist Charlotte, whom the researcher asked to advertise her technology, offered her an alternative use for the device. The "Kamera Lens for Image Recognition Sample Collection" was specially designed for high-fidelity image capture and analysis. The rapid focal length adjustment could be a very useful function in its own right. It would make journalists' jobs much easier and had the potential to revolutionize Fontaine's news media. Thus, Lepine-Pauline regained her hope of becoming rich, and Charlotte got news material: _"The boundaries between real news reports and news-like fiction must not be blurred, even when there's a compelling justification for doing so."_

![Image 203: Two video game characters standing near table with blue parasol in the game Genshin Impact](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/08/10/237301566/39898952871795c3e8ea05e27fbe71d0_3260572697202661017.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

One of the Lil' Fungi's Fun-Tastic Fiesta events, Fungus Mechanicus, took place in the Court of Fontaine, organized by the Fungi trainer, Haniyyah, and her writer friend Souka. Haniyyah had come to Fontaine to search for reliable investors for the official Fungi tournament, and to host a preview event to advertise the Fungi's cuteness and attract an audience in advance. Haniyyah also wanted to find researchers from the Institute to make a new Wisdom Orb that would allow humans to tame the Fungi. The Fontaine Research Institute's Fonta research team didn't just provide a huge amount of funding to Haniyyah and Souka, but they also promised to help them look for the necessary talent.

![Image 204: Blue and red elemental beings and a gold staff are in a dungeon](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/08/10/237301566/33ea1ef3bf0e4c75b6b4fc03851a6a00_5803941814721915785.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

Souka prepared preview event plans, ordered elegant clothes, and trained the Eremite Haniyyah to improve her speech and manners. In the new competition, people were directing Fungi to defeat all the Mechanici. The game received a pretty good initial response, but it was lacking in long-term potential, so it quickly lost popularity, so Souka combined elements from various documents and fiction to change the Mechanici into pieces that simulate powerful opponents, which adds all manner of variables to the game. She also went to The Steambird to discuss the possibility of placing an advertisement in the newspaper to popularize the game. Turenna, a member of the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol, was put in charge of monitoring the exotic animals brought to Fontaine from abroad, as well as providing highly skilled assistance to Haniyyah and Souka. The Traveler and Paimon's friends, Bongo-Head and Kindlejoy, were even assigned special people to take care of them.

**Court of Fontaine: Court Region Waterway Hub**
------------------------------------------------
![Image 255: Two characters standing in front of a large building](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/08/10/237301566/a24cba7dd104e1365af9cb2a2d3fcb57_1784185875136257588.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

The Waterway Hub is located on the square in the Court of Fontaine with the fountain. The elevator connects the Palais Mermonia and the Clementine aquabus line leading to Romaritime Harbor. The third line, the Callas line, leading to the Research Institute, was damaged during the explosion of the Central Laboratory. The President of Spina di Rosula, Navia, is planning to restore the Callas line. The main hall of the station is on the first level out of four, the Clementine line is on the second, and on the third level is the Navia line leading to the Erinnyes. At the Waterway Hub, Certified Players, Rhemia, and Pruniere can be found. Rhemia is a Melusine who serves in the Marechaussee Phantom and is quite interested in the humans around. Rhemia has recently begun playing Genius Invokation TCG with passersby, engaging in friendly conversation with them as well. The prowess she displays in these matches has earned her a lot of respect. Pruniere is an Aquabus Maintenance Worker who ensures the integrity of the waterways. After finishing the basic water maintenance work, Pruniere still has a surfeit of free time, and thus has developed superb skill at playing Genius Invokation TCG.

**Court of Fontaine: Vasari Passage**
-------------------------------------
![Image 266: An open-air courtyard in a fantasy location, where a fountain with a clock on top serves as the focal point](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/08/10/237301566/6cfb7c362da88be0304d8e27ed1611f4_8515396456660773810.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

In the main square of the Court of Fontaine, in the Vasari Passage, a large moving fountain and the Court of Fontaine Waterway Hub are situated. Certified Player Paban can be found here. He is a newsy who sells The Steambird and is considered the Court of Fontaine's own miniature "Know-It-All" by some others his age. Paban has recently taken to playing Genius Invokation TCG with those who come to him for information, offering them the following deal: If he wins, his opponent must become his distributor.

![Image 267: Interior of a forge in Genshin Impact with a woman wearing a dress, a light blue sun umbrella over a table and a forge oven on the background](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/08/10/237301566/801a698ae9cc26ea45ef2c270e6e3940_4386840058207535060.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

In addition, various merchants can be found in the passage, such as a fruit vendor and Certified Player, Eugenie, a manager of a snack shop, Louis, and Boucicaut from Damoville Purveyor. Next to the Gallery is the building where the rival of the famous fashion designer, Chiori, lives. When he falsely accused Chiori of collaborating with criminals, she called the captain of the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol, Chevreuse, to prevent Chiori from overdoing it in the "conversation." The Beaumont Workshop, owned by Estelle, is also located there. The workshop offers a full, comprehensive service for individual orders. To order, prepayment, documentation with requirements, and supporting documents are required. Forging in the workshop is carried out by a special machine running on Indemnitium. Previously, during trials, the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale collected people's faith in justice and converted it into energy, which was then used throughout Fontaine. In addition to Indemnitium, Fontaine has Pneumousia energy, which is produced independently of the Archon's power but is unstable in nature. When Fontaine's prophecy had not yet come true, Estelle helped the Fatui make Magic Pockets in which people could put all their things in case of danger. At the time, Estelle owed money to Confrerie of Cabriere. She promised to repay her debt by the end of the month, but the people from Confrerie of Cabriere wanted to get seventy percent at that moment. It turned out that Confrerie of Cabriere owed money to the Northland Bank. The Fatui Harbinger Childe went to collect their debt and stopped to talk to the Traveler returning from visiting Estelle.

When Furina left her role as Archon, she quickly left her residence and went to live in a small apartment. Although she had gained her freedom and fulfilled her duty, she did not know where to go next. The concept of "freedom" rang hollow. Furina's luggage remained piled up in her new rental apartment, and she lacked all will even to tidy up or get moved in. All she could do was lie in bed and stare at the bare ceiling. One day, Clorinde the Champion Duelist, who had previously been under her command, visited her. The duelist was shocked at Furina's living conditions, quickly expressing her willingness to pay for better accommodations, a notion Furina expended no small amount of effort disabusing her of. Despite this, she was dragged, however reluctantly, into at least properly unpacking and tidying up the room, and now Furina lives in the Vasari Passage.

![Image 268: Furina, Paimon, and Aether stand in a room surrounded by people, with one person pointing his finger](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/08/10/237301566/d90722a98eaae5cab9646b02768c11f0_5204605889212720370.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

Not far from this apartment was the meeting place of the theater troupe that Furina helped once. After she became an ordinary person, she never wanted to go on stage again, but after learning about the history of the troupe, she decided to become an artistic consultant for the last time in the play "The Little Oceanid." The main actress, suffering from illness, was unable to appear in the final scene of the play, so Furina had to replace her. After a wonderful performance and communication with the troupe, Furina decided that perhaps she would return to the world of theater.

One day, the Chief Editor of The Steambird, Euphrasie, told the Traveler about an order that had been kept in the editorial office for six months. In the order, an elderly man, Benoit Leroy, asked to find assistants. When Traveler and Paimon volunteered for the task, they saw Benoit looking depressed and scared next to his daughter, Morticia's, husband. After investigating and talking with Morticia and her husband, it turned out that Morticia's real name was Autumn, and Benoit was her adoptive father, who sold her as a wife to a rich man for the sake of inheritance. When Autumn's first husband died, Benoit received that house in the Vasari Passage and gave his daughter to her second husband, with whom she had a daughter. Later, Autumn killed her husband, for which she was sent to the Fortress of Meropide, and her daughter remained with Benoit. He gave the girl up for adoption without saying a word to Autumn. Autumn and her "husband," Athos, escaped from prison to take revenge on Benoit and find the girl, but even after learning the truth, Autumn did not dare to invade the happy life of her daughter. Molli was adopted by a caring and rich family who tried to protect her from Benoit.

![Image 269: The scene is a vibrant outdoor cafe area with azure umbrellas, tables, and chairs set against a backdrop of elegant architecture and meticulously manicured greenery](https://act-upload.hoyoverse.com/event-ugc-hoyowiki/2024/08/10/237301566/8be337374863e51ac0106d639321cc40_4168802507035523802.png?x-oss-process=image%2Fformat%2Cwebp)

In this place, the Café Lutece is located, owned by Arouet. He previously worked in the Maison Gestion, and his views there were considered quite radical. When Arouet got tired of work, he quit to open a cafe. Now he is a coffee maker of the highest level. Café Lutece is the most popular сafé in the Vasari Passage, its delicious coffee and snacks earning plaudits from customers from all backgrounds to freely and comfortably discuss philosophy and other topics as they enjoy their coffee. Anyone may participate, and no topic is forbidden, with the exception of "death."
